**[BEFORE THE BOARD OF SUPERVISORS OF CONESTOGA TOWNSHIP, LANCASTER COUNTY, PENNSYLVANIA]{.underline}**

**In Re: Conditional Use Application of Pinnacle Renewables LLC and Brightfield Solar Project LLC for a Solar Energy System Exceeding 10 MW and Accessory Battery Energy Storage System**

Application No.: **CU-2024-006**

Filed: **June 3, 2024**

**DECISION AND ORDER**

Date of Decision: **December 6, 2024**

**[I. PROCEDURAL HISTORY]{.underline}**

The Board of Supervisors of Conestoga Township, Lancaster County, Pennsylvania (the \"Board\"), hereby sets forth the procedural history of this matter as follows:

1\. On June 3, 2024, Pinnacle Renewables LLC (\"Applicant\"), a Delaware limited liability company with principal offices at 4200 Commerce Parkway, Suite 310, Wilmington, DE 19801, and its wholly owned subsidiary Brightfield Solar Project LLC (\"Project Company\"), a Pennsylvania limited liability company formed on March 15, 2024, with registered agent Statehouse Registered Agents, Inc., 1500 Market Street, Suite 700, Philadelphia, PA 19102, filed a Conditional Use Application with the Conestoga Township Board of Supervisors seeking approval for the construction and operation of a ground-mounted solar energy generating system with an alternating current nameplate capacity of 120 MW, together with an accessory battery energy storage system with a capacity of 40 MW / 160 MWh, on approximately 850 acres situated within the Agricultural-Rural (A-R) zoning district of Conestoga Township (the \"Application\").

2\. The Application was filed pursuant to Section 27-605(B)(14) of the Conestoga Township Zoning Ordinance, Chapter 27, as amended December 2023 (the \"Ordinance\"), which classifies solar energy systems exceeding 10 MW of nameplate generating capacity as a \"Conditional Use\" in the Agricultural-Rural (A-R) zoning district, subject to specific standards and conditions as may be imposed by the Board.

3\. The Applicant was represented throughout these proceedings by Christine Navarro, Esquire, of Hathaway & Lowell LLP, 1700 Arch Street, Suite 2200, Philadelphia, PA 19103. Derek Holcomb, Vice President of Development of Pinnacle Renewables LLC, served as the primary project contact and appeared at all public hearings on behalf of the Applicant.

4\. In accordance with the Pennsylvania Municipalities Planning Code, Act of July 31, 1968, P.L. 805, as amended, 53 P.S. §§ 10101 *et seq.* (the \"MPC\"), the Application was referred to the Lancaster County Planning Commission for review and advisory recommendation. Thomas Reinhart, Director of Planning for the Lancaster County Planning Commission, oversaw the review. Barbara Kreider served as Zoning Hearing Officer for the Lancaster County Planning Commission during its consideration of the Application. On July 22, 2024, the Lancaster County Planning Commission issued its advisory (non-binding) recommendation, finding the Application generally consistent with the Lancaster County Comprehensive Plan and recommending approval subject to certain conditions and recommendations.

5\. The Township retained the following consultants to assist in its review of the Application:

> \(a\) Fieldstone Engineering Associates, through Gregory Shultz, P.E., of 220 Centerville Road, Lancaster, PA 17601, as Township Engineer, to review the technical submissions, including the Site Plan, stormwater management plan, grading plan, and engineering specifications;
>
> \(b\) Clarendon Appraisal Group, through Michael Engstrom, MAI, to prepare an independent property value impact assessment evaluating the potential effect of the proposed project on values of adjacent non-participating properties.

6\. The Applicant\'s environmental and permitting consultants were Ridgepoint Environmental Consultants LLC, through Priya Mukherjee, Lead Consultant, of 88 Greenway Boulevard, Suite 105, King of Prussia, PA 19406, which prepared the Phase I Environmental Site Assessment, Cultural Resources Survey, Pennsylvania Natural Diversity Inventory review, and related environmental documentation submitted in support of the Application.

7\. Three public hearings were duly noticed and conducted by the Board of Supervisors in accordance with the notice and hearing requirements of the MPC and the Ordinance:

> \(a\) **Public Hearing No. 1** was held on August 14, 2024, at which the Applicant presented an overview of the proposed project, introduced its expert witnesses, and submitted its initial exhibits. The Township Engineer and Township Solicitor were present and participated. Members of the public were afforded the opportunity to ask questions and provide testimony.
>
> \(b\) **Public Hearing No. 2** was held on September 11, 2024, at which the Applicant presented additional technical evidence, including the noise study, glare assessment, decommissioning plan, and property value analysis. Adjacent property owners and members of the public provided testimony in opposition to and in support of the Application. Cross-examination of expert witnesses occurred.
>
> \(c\) **Public Hearing No. 3** was held on October 9, 2024, at which the Applicant presented rebuttal testimony, the Township Engineer presented his findings and recommendations, and the Clarendon Appraisal Group presented its property value impact assessment. The public hearing record was closed at the conclusion of this hearing.

8\. Testimony was received over the course of the three hearings from the Applicant and its representatives, adjacent property owners, and expert witnesses, including licensed professional engineers, environmental consultants, acoustical engineers, real estate appraisers, and agricultural specialists. All testimony was taken under oath, and a verbatim transcript of each hearing was prepared by the court reporter.

9\. Following the close of the evidentiary record, the Board of Supervisors deliberated in public session. On November 18, 2024, the Board voted three (3) in favor and two (2) opposed to grant conditional use approval for the Brightfield Solar Project, subject to the conditions set forth herein. Chair Harold Zimmerman, Supervisor Raymond Eckert, and Supervisor Linda Groff voted in favor. Supervisor Karen Beiler and Supervisor Jonas Lapp voted against the Application.

10\. This written Decision and Order is issued on December 6, 2024. The thirty (30) day appeal period under the MPC, 53 P.S. § 11002-A, commences on the date of this Decision and expires on January 5, 2025.

**[II. PROJECT DESCRIPTION]{.underline}**

Based upon the Application materials, testimony presented at the public hearings, and the evidentiary record, the Board finds the proposed project to be described as follows:

**Project Name.** The project is designated the \"Brightfield Solar Project\" (the \"Project\").

**Technology.** The Project will employ single-axis tracking photovoltaic solar panel technology. The facility will consist of approximately 296,000 individual solar modules arranged on single-axis tracker systems that orient the panels to follow the path of the sun during daylight hours. Electrical conversion will be accomplished through approximately 40 string inverters and 3 central power conversion stations located within the project site. The single-axis tracking technology maximizes energy production by optimizing the angle of incidence of sunlight upon the photovoltaic cells throughout the day.

**Nameplate Capacity.** The Project will have a nameplate generating capacity of 120 megawatts alternating current (MW AC) and 156 megawatts direct current (MW DC), yielding a DC-to-AC ratio of approximately 1.30. The DC overbuild relative to AC capacity is standard industry practice designed to maximize the utilization of the inverter and interconnection infrastructure and to optimize energy production across varying irradiance conditions.

**Battery Energy Storage System (BESS).** The Application includes an optional battery energy storage system (BESS) as a secondary and accessory use to the solar generating facility. The proposed BESS has a capacity of 40 MW / 160 MWh, meaning it can discharge at a rate of 40 megawatts for up to four hours. The BESS will utilize lithium-ion battery technology housed in modular containerized units sited within the project boundary. The BESS is intended to store excess solar energy production for dispatch during periods of peak demand or grid need.

**Project Area.** The Project encompasses approximately 850 acres across seven (7) contiguous parcels, all of which are situated within the Agricultural-Rural (A-R) zoning district of Conestoga Township. The total fenced project area will be approximately 720 acres, with the remaining acreage devoted to setbacks, vegetative buffers, access roads, and stormwater management facilities. The actual area covered by solar panels (the \"panel coverage area\") will be approximately 580 acres.

**Interconnection.** The Project will interconnect to the regional electrical grid at a 138 kilovolt (kV) point of interconnection at the existing Conestoga Substation, located approximately 2.3 miles from the project site. A new generation tie line (\"gen-tie line\") will be constructed to connect the project\'s on-site substation to the Conestoga Substation. The Applicant holds interconnection queue position AG2-2024-0847 with Mid-Atlantic Grid Coordination LLC, the regional transmission organization responsible for managing interconnection requests in the applicable service territory.

**Estimated Construction Cost.** The total estimated construction cost for the Project is \$200 million, consisting of approximately \$168 million for the solar generating facility and approximately \$32 million for the battery energy storage system.

**Construction and Commercial Operation Timeline.** The Applicant has identified a target construction start date of April 1, 2026, with a projected commercial operation date of December 31, 2027. These dates are subject to the Applicant\'s timely satisfaction of the conditions imposed herein, as well as receipt of all necessary federal, state, and county permits and approvals.

**Estimated Annual Tax Revenue.** The Project is estimated to generate approximately \$427,000 per year in total tax revenue to the Township, consisting of \$385,000 per year under a negotiated Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) agreement and approximately \$42,000 per year in real estate taxes on non-exempt improvements.

**Parcel Information.** The seven (7) parcels comprising the Project site, the respective landowners, acreages, and lease terms are as follows:

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Parcel ID**     **Owner**                      **Acres**         **Lease Term**
  ----------------- ------------------------------ ----------------- ------------------------------------
  120-45-001        Elmer J. & Ruth A. Stoltzfus   185.3             35 years + two 5-year extensions

  120-45-002        Stoltzfus Family Trust         142.7             35 years + two 5-year extensions

  120-45-003        Brubaker Agricultural LLC      210.4             30 years + three 5-year extensions

  120-45-004        Brubaker Agricultural LLC      98.6              30 years + three 5-year extensions

  120-45-005        David M. Herr                  75.2              35 years + two 5-year extensions

  120-45-006        Lancaster Heritage Land Co.    88.9              30 years + two 5-year extensions

  120-45-007        Lancaster Heritage Land Co.    48.9              30 years + two 5-year extensions

  **Total**                                        **850.0**         
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Applicant has represented that all land lease agreements have been fully executed between the respective landowners and Brightfield Solar Project LLC. Lease documentation, including memoranda of lease suitable for recording, has been verified by Commonwealth Title & Escrow LLC. All seven parcels are located within the Agricultural-Rural (A-R) zoning district of Conestoga Township, as confirmed by the Township Zoning Officer.

**[III. FINDINGS OF FACT]{.underline}**

Based upon the Application, the testimony and evidence presented at the public hearings, the reports and recommendations of the Township Engineer, the advisory recommendation of the Lancaster County Planning Commission, the property value impact assessment prepared by the Clarendon Appraisal Group, and the entire record in this matter, the Board makes the following Findings of Fact:

**A. Application and Zoning Compliance**

**Finding 1.** The Application was properly filed on June 3, 2024, accompanied by all required application materials, filing fees, and supporting documentation as specified by the Ordinance. The Application was deemed complete by the Township Zoning Officer and accepted for processing.

**Finding 2.** The Project site, comprising all seven (7) parcels identified in the Application and described in Section II of this Decision, is located entirely within the Agricultural-Rural (A-R) zoning district of Conestoga Township, as depicted on the official Conestoga Township Zoning Map, last amended December 2023.

**Finding 3.** Solar energy systems exceeding 10 MW of nameplate generating capacity are expressly permitted as a Conditional Use within the Agricultural-Rural (A-R) zoning district under Section 27-605(B)(14) of the Conestoga Township Zoning Ordinance, as amended December 2023. Battery energy storage systems operated as accessory uses to approved solar energy systems are likewise addressed within the same section of the Ordinance.

**Finding 4.** The Lancaster County Planning Commission, through its Director of Planning Thomas Reinhart and Zoning Hearing Officer Barbara Kreider, reviewed the Application in accordance with its statutory advisory review obligations under the MPC. On July 22, 2024, the Lancaster County Planning Commission issued its advisory recommendation, finding the Application generally consistent with the Lancaster County Comprehensive Plan, including the Plan\'s goals for economic development, environmental stewardship, and responsible siting of renewable energy facilities. The Lancaster County Planning Commission recommended approval of the Application subject to certain conditions and recommendations regarding setbacks, screening, stormwater management, and decommissioning assurances.

**Finding 5.** Three public hearings were duly noticed and conducted in accordance with the notice and hearing requirements of the MPC and the Ordinance on August 14, 2024, September 11, 2024, and October 9, 2024. Legal notice of each hearing was published in the *Lancaster Intelligencer Journal* and the *Lancaster New Era* at least fifteen (15) days prior to each hearing. Individual notice was provided by first class mail to all property owners within 500 feet of the project boundary. All hearings were open to the public, and all interested parties were afforded the opportunity to present testimony, cross-examine witnesses, and submit documentary evidence.

**B. Site and Design**

**Finding 6.** The Project site comprises 850.0 acres across seven (7) contiguous parcels, all of which are under fully executed lease agreements between the respective landowners and Brightfield Solar Project LLC, as the project-specific special purpose entity and wholly owned subsidiary of Pinnacle Renewables LLC. The lease terms range from thirty (30) to thirty-five (35) years, with extension options of two to three additional five-year terms, as set forth in Section II of this Decision.

**Finding 7.** The proposed facility design, as depicted on the Site Plan dated September 1, 2024, prepared by Ridgepoint Environmental Consultants LLC in coordination with the Applicant\'s engineering team and submitted as Applicant\'s Exhibit A-1, satisfies the dimensional requirements of the Ordinance for the Agricultural-Rural (A-R) zoning district, including minimum lot area, minimum lot width, maximum building coverage, and maximum impervious surface coverage requirements. The Township Engineer, Gregory Shultz, P.E., confirmed in his review letter dated September 30, 2024, that the Site Plan demonstrates compliance with all applicable dimensional standards.

**Finding 8.** The proposed solar panel height at maximum tilt is 14.5 feet above finished grade, which is below the 20-foot maximum height permitted for solar energy systems under Section 27-605(B)(14)(d) of the Ordinance. The central power conversion stations and project substation structures will have maximum heights of approximately 25 feet and 45 feet, respectively, which are within the height limits established for accessory structures associated with conditional uses in the A-R district.

**Finding 9.** The proposed setbacks for solar panels, inverters, and substations, as shown on the Site Plan dated September 1, 2024, meet or exceed the minimum setback requirements specified in Section 27-605(B)(14)(e) of the Ordinance. The Applicant has demonstrated compliance with the required setbacks from non-participating property lines, public road rights-of-way, and occupied dwellings on non-participating parcels.

**Finding 10.** The proposed perimeter fencing is seven (7) feet in height and will be constructed of chain-link or comparable security fencing materials surrounding the entire fenced project area of approximately 720 acres. Wildlife passage openings measuring not less than six (6) inches in height and twelve (12) inches in width will be installed at intervals of no more than 500 feet along the fence line, consistent with the requirements of Section 27-605(B)(14)(g) of the Ordinance and best management practices for wildlife corridor management.

**C. Environmental and Natural Resources**

**Finding 11.** A Phase I Environmental Site Assessment was completed in May 2024 in accordance with ASTM Standard E1527-21 by Ridgepoint Environmental Consultants LLC. The Phase I ESA identified no Recognized Environmental Conditions (RECs), Controlled Recognized Environmental Conditions (CRECs), or Historical Recognized Environmental Conditions (HRECs) on any of the seven (7) parcels comprising the Project site. The Assessment concluded that there are no known environmental liabilities associated with the Project site that would impair its development for the proposed use.

**Finding 12.** A Cultural Resources Survey was completed by Ridgepoint Environmental Consultants LLC in April 2024 in accordance with the guidelines of the Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission (PHMC). The survey identified one potentially eligible historic resource within the project\'s area of potential effect: the Stoltzfus Farmstead, dating to circa 1847, located within approximately 200 feet of the project boundary on Parcel 120-45-001. The Stoltzfus Farmstead includes a stone farmhouse, a bank barn, and several outbuildings that may be eligible for listing on the National Register of Historic Places. Formal consultation with the PHMC regarding the project\'s potential effects on this resource is required and has not yet been completed as of the date of this Decision.

**Finding 13.** A Pennsylvania Natural Diversity Inventory (PNDI) review was conducted by Ridgepoint Environmental Consultants LLC and identified potential habitat for the bog turtle (*Glyptemys muhlenbergii*), a species listed as threatened under the federal Endangered Species Act and endangered under Pennsylvania law, on parcels 120-45-003 and 120-45-004. The PNDI results indicate that a Phase 2 bog turtle habitat assessment and, if warranted, Phase 3 presence/absence surveys may be required. Formal consultation with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and the Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission is required and has not yet been completed as of the date of this Decision.

**Finding 14.** The Project site contains approximately 623 acres of prime agricultural land as classified by the United States Department of Agriculture Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS). This classification is based upon soil survey data and land capability classifications identifying soils of prime farmland quality on the relevant parcels. The balance of the 850-acre project site consists of soils classified as farmland of statewide importance, woodland, or other non-prime categories.

**Finding 15.** The Applicant has submitted a preliminary stormwater management plan prepared in accordance with the Conestoga Township Stormwater Management Ordinance and the Lancaster County Act 167 Stormwater Management Plan. The Township Engineer, Gregory Shultz, P.E., has reviewed the preliminary plan and provided comments dated October 1, 2024, identifying several items requiring revision and additional detail in the final submission. A final stormwater management plan, incorporating the Township Engineer\'s comments and approved by the Lancaster County Conservation District, is required prior to commencement of any construction activity.

**D. Economic and Community Impact**

**Finding 16.** The estimated total construction cost of the Project is approximately \$200 million, consisting of approximately \$168 million for the solar generating facility and approximately \$32 million for the battery energy storage system. The Applicant testified that the Project will create approximately 350-400 construction jobs during the peak construction period and approximately 8-12 permanent full-time equivalent operational and maintenance positions.

**Finding 17.** The Applicant and the Township have negotiated preliminary terms for a Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) agreement providing for annual payments of \$385,000 per year for Years 1 through 15 of commercial operation, with a 2% annual escalator commencing thereafter for the remaining term of the PILOT agreement. As of the date of this Decision, a formal PILOT agreement has not yet been executed by the parties. The PILOT terms remain subject to finalization and execution in a form satisfactory to the Township Solicitor.

**Finding 18.** Total estimated annual tax revenue to the Township from the Project is approximately \$427,000, consisting of \$385,000 per year under the negotiated PILOT terms and approximately \$42,000 per year in real estate taxes assessed on non-exempt improvements associated with the facility, including substations, power conversion stations, and operations and maintenance buildings.

**Finding 19.** The Township retained the Clarendon Appraisal Group, through Michael Engstrom, MAI, a Pennsylvania-certified general real estate appraiser, to prepare an independent property value impact assessment. The Clarendon Appraisal Group reviewed comparable paired sales data, conducted site inspections, and analyzed peer-reviewed academic literature on the subject of utility-scale solar facilities and adjacent property values. The appraisal report, dated September 25, 2024, concluded that the Project, subject to compliance with the screening and setback requirements of the Ordinance and this Decision, would have no material negative impact on the market values of adjacent non-participating properties. The report noted that the weight of available empirical evidence does not support a finding of systematic property value diminution attributable to proximity to utility-scale solar facilities when appropriate screening and setback measures are in place.

**Finding 20.** The Applicant submitted a noise impact study prepared by Harris Acoustics Group, a qualified acoustical engineering firm. The noise study was conducted using the methodology set forth in ANSI/ASA S12.9-2013/Part 2 and employed industry-standard predictive noise modeling software. The study concluded that projected operational noise levels from the solar tracking systems, inverters, and substation transformers would not exceed 45 dBA at any non-participating property line under worst-case operating conditions. The 45 dBA threshold is the maximum operational noise level permitted under the Ordinance.

**E. Decommissioning and Financial Assurances**

**Finding 21.** The Applicant submitted a Decommissioning Plan and Cost Estimate prepared by Ridgepoint Environmental Consultants LLC under the supervision of a licensed professional engineer. The Decommissioning Plan provides for the complete removal of all above-ground and below-ground project infrastructure to a depth of thirty-six (36) inches, the restoration of disturbed areas to pre-construction agricultural conditions, and the disposal or recycling of all removed materials in accordance with applicable law. The estimated gross decommissioning cost is \$8,400,000, the estimated salvage value of project components is \$2,100,000, and the resulting net decommissioning cost is \$6,300,000.

**Finding 22.** Under Section 27-605(B)(14)(k) of the Ordinance, the Applicant is required to post decommissioning security in the amount of not less than one hundred twenty-five percent (125%) of the estimated net decommissioning cost. Based upon the net decommissioning cost of \$6,300,000, the required decommissioning security is \$7,875,000 (i.e., \$6,300,000 × 1.25 = \$7,875,000).

**Finding 23.** Acceptable forms of decommissioning security under the Ordinance include a surety bond from a surety company authorized to do business in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, an irrevocable letter of credit issued by a financial institution rated A- or better by Standard & Poor\'s or the equivalent rating from Moody\'s or Fitch, or an escrow account held by a financial institution meeting the same rating requirement.

**Finding 24.** The Applicant has identified Northbrook Surety Company as a potential surety bond provider for the decommissioning security. The Applicant has not yet submitted a commitment letter or draft surety bond instrument for review by the Township. The final form and sufficiency of the decommissioning security shall be subject to review and approval by the Township Solicitor.

**Finding 25.** The Applicant has proposed an agricultural mitigation payment to Lancaster Farmland Trust, a qualified land conservation organization operating in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, to mitigate the temporary removal of prime agricultural land from active agricultural production. The agricultural mitigation payment is intended to fund farmland preservation efforts in Lancaster County during the operational life of the Project.

**[IV. CONCLUSIONS OF LAW]{.underline}**

Based upon the foregoing Findings of Fact and the entire record in this matter, the Board reaches the following Conclusions of Law:

**Conclusion 1.** The Board of Supervisors of Conestoga Township has jurisdiction over this Conditional Use Application pursuant to Section 27-605 of the Conestoga Township Zoning Ordinance and Section 603(c) of the Pennsylvania Municipalities Planning Code, 53 P.S. § 10603(c). The Conditional Use Application was properly filed, noticed, and heard in accordance with all procedural requirements of the MPC and the Ordinance, and the Board has the authority to grant or deny the Application and to impose reasonable conditions upon any approval.

**Conclusion 2.** The Applicant has met its burden under the MPC of demonstrating that the proposed use satisfies the specific objective standards and criteria set forth in Section 27-605(B)(14) of the Ordinance for solar energy systems exceeding 10 MW in the Agricultural-Rural (A-R) zoning district. The evidence of record establishes that the proposed Project, as designed and conditioned, meets the requirements for lot area, setbacks, height, fencing, screening, noise, decommissioning, and other dimensional and operational standards specified in the Ordinance.

**Conclusion 3.** Pursuant to established Pennsylvania case law, including *Bray v. Zoning Board of Adjustment*, 410 A.2d 909 (Pa. Commw. Ct. 1980), and *South Whitehall Township v. City of Allentown*, 675 A.2d 323 (Pa. Commw. Ct. 1996), the Applicant, having satisfied the specific objective requirements of the Ordinance, is presumptively entitled to conditional use approval. The burden then shifts to objectors to demonstrate, by substantial evidence, that the proposed use will have a detrimental impact on the health, safety, and welfare of the community that is greater than that normally expected from the type of use and that cannot be adequately mitigated by the imposition of reasonable conditions.

**Conclusion 4.** The evidence presented by objectors at the public hearings regarding potential impacts on property values, noise, glare, visual aesthetics, and the agricultural character of the surrounding area does not rise to the level of substantial evidence sufficient to overcome the Applicant\'s presumptive entitlement to approval. The Board credits the expert testimony and empirical studies submitted by the Applicant and the Township\'s independent consultants, including the Clarendon Appraisal Group property value impact assessment and the Harris Acoustics Group noise study, over the lay testimony and anecdotal concerns expressed by objectors. The Board finds that the impacts cited by objectors are either speculative, unsupported by competent evidence, or adequately addressed through the conditions imposed herein.

**Conclusion 5.** The conditions imposed in this Decision are necessary to protect the public health, safety, and welfare of the community, to mitigate the potential impacts of the proposed use on neighboring properties and the surrounding environment, and to ensure that the proposed use operates in a manner consistent with the standards of the Ordinance. Each condition is reasonably related to a specific identified impact of the proposed use.

**Conclusion 6.** The proposed Project is consistent with the goals and objectives of the Conestoga Township Comprehensive Plan, last updated in 2021, including the Plan\'s provisions regarding economic development, agricultural preservation, environmental stewardship, and community resilience. The proposed Project is also consistent with the Lancaster County Comprehensive Plan, as confirmed by the advisory recommendation of the Lancaster County Planning Commission dated July 22, 2024.

**Conclusion 7.** The conditions set forth in this Decision are authorized under Section 603(c)(2) of the MPC, 53 P.S. § 10603(c)(2), which empowers the governing body to attach such reasonable conditions and safeguards as it may deem necessary to implement the purposes of the MPC and the Ordinance, and under the specific conditional use standards of Section 27-605(B)(14) of the Ordinance.

**Conclusion 8.** This Decision is supported by substantial evidence in the record, including the Application and supporting materials, testimony of witnesses at the public hearings, expert reports and studies, the advisory recommendation of the Lancaster County Planning Commission, the review findings and recommendations of the Township Engineer, and the property value impact assessment prepared by the Clarendon Appraisal Group.

**[V. ORDER]{.underline}**

**NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY ORDERED AND DECREED** by the Board of Supervisors of Conestoga Township, Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, this 6th day of December, 2024, that the Conditional Use Application filed by Pinnacle Renewables LLC and Brightfield Solar Project LLC, Application No. CU-2024-006, for the construction and operation of the Brightfield Solar Project, a 120 MW AC ground-mounted solar energy generating system with an accessory 40 MW / 160 MWh battery energy storage system, on approximately 850 acres within the Agricultural-Rural (A-R) zoning district of Conestoga Township, is **GRANTED**, subject to the following conditions:

**[VI. CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL]{.underline}**

**Category A: Site Design and Layout**

**Condition 1 --- General Compliance.** The Project shall be designed, constructed, and operated in substantial conformance with the Site Plan dated September 1, 2024, prepared by Ridgepoint Environmental Consultants LLC and submitted as Applicant\'s Exhibit A-1, and all application materials submitted in support of the Conditional Use Application, as the same may be modified by the conditions set forth herein. In the event of any conflict between the Application materials and this Decision and Order, the terms and conditions of this Decision and Order shall control.

**Condition 2 --- Applicant Entity.** Brightfield Solar Project LLC, as the project-specific special purpose entity wholly owned by Pinnacle Renewables LLC, shall be the responsible entity for compliance with all conditions of this Decision and Order. Pinnacle Renewables LLC shall provide a parent guaranty of Brightfield Solar Project LLC\'s obligations under this Decision, in a form and substance satisfactory to the Township Solicitor, prior to issuance of any building permit. Said parent guaranty shall remain in effect for the duration of the Project\'s operational life and through completion of decommissioning.

**Condition 3 --- Lease Verification.** Prior to issuance of any building permit, the Applicant shall provide to the Township executed copies of all land lease agreements, or duly executed memoranda thereof in recordable form, for each of the seven (7) project parcels identified in Section II of this Decision, together with evidence of recording in the Lancaster County Recorder of Deeds, demonstrating that the Applicant has the legal right to develop, construct, and operate the solar energy facility on each parcel for the full lease term, including any extension periods.

**Condition 4 --- Scope of Approval.** This conditional use approval covers only the Project site as depicted on the Site Plan dated September 1, 2024, comprising approximately 850 acres across the seven (7) parcels identified in the Application. The approval does not extend to any facilities, structures, or improvements located outside the boundaries of the approved Project site as depicted on the Site Plan. Any development activities outside the approved project site boundary shall require separate land use approvals as applicable under the Ordinance, the MPC, or any other applicable law or regulation.

**Condition 5 --- Setbacks (Panels).** All solar panels shall maintain the following minimum setbacks, measured from the nearest edge of the panel at maximum tilt:

> \(a\) One hundred (100) feet from any non-participating property line;
>
> \(b\) One hundred fifty (150) feet from the edge of any public road right-of-way;
>
> \(c\) Five hundred (500) feet from any occupied dwelling located on a non-participating parcel.

These setbacks are in addition to any other applicable setback requirements of the Ordinance and shall be maintained for the operational life of the Project.

**Condition 6 --- Setbacks (Substation/Inverters).** All substations and central power conversion stations shall maintain a minimum setback of two hundred fifty (250) feet from any non-participating property line. String inverters mounted on or adjacent to the tracker rows are exempt from this requirement and shall instead comply with the panel setback requirements set forth in Condition 5.

**Condition 7 --- Access Roads.** Internal access roads within the Project site shall be constructed of compacted gravel or equivalent material of sufficient bearing capacity and width to accommodate emergency vehicle access, including fire apparatus. The minimum width of internal access roads shall be sixteen (16) feet. The primary construction access point shall be located on Hershey Mill Road at a location approved by the Township Engineer and shall be designed to accommodate turning movements for heavy construction vehicles. A Traffic Management Plan shall be prepared by a qualified traffic engineer and submitted to the Township Engineer for review and approval not less than sixty (60) days prior to commencement of construction. The Traffic Management Plan shall address haul routes, vehicle staging areas, traffic control measures, and any temporary road closures or detours.

**Category B: Environmental and Natural Resources**

**Condition 8 --- Threatened and Endangered Species Consultation.** The Applicant shall complete all necessary federal and state threatened and endangered species consultations, including but not limited to the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Phase 2 and, if warranted, Phase 3 bog turtle survey protocols, prior to any land disturbance on parcels 120-45-003 and 120-45-004. Written confirmation of completed consultation, together with copies of all correspondence and any required avoidance, minimization, or mitigation measures issued by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and the Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission, shall be provided to the Township prior to issuance of a grading permit for those parcels. No grading, clearing, or vegetation removal shall occur on parcels 120-45-003 or 120-45-004 until this condition has been satisfied in full.

**Condition 9 --- Historic Resource Consultation (PHMC).** Prior to issuance of any grading permit for the Project, the Applicant shall obtain and submit to the Township written confirmation from the Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission (PHMC) that the Project will have no adverse effect on the Stoltzfus Farmstead (circa 1847) or any other eligible or listed historic resource identified within the project\'s area of potential effect, as determined through the Section 106 consultation process or equivalent state-level review. The written confirmation shall be in a form acceptable to the Township Solicitor and shall demonstrate that the PHMC concurs with a finding of no adverse effect.

**Condition 10 --- Stormwater Management Plan Submission.** The Applicant shall submit a final stormwater management plan, prepared in accordance with the Conestoga Township Stormwater Management Ordinance and the Lancaster County Act 167 Stormwater Management Plan, to the Township Engineer for review and approval within ninety (90) days of the date of this Decision. The ninety-day period shall expire on March 6, 2025.

**Condition 11 --- Stormwater Plan --- Conservation District Approval Required First.** The stormwater management plan submitted to the Township Engineer under Condition 10 shall have been previously reviewed and approved by the Lancaster County Conservation District. Evidence of Lancaster County Conservation District approval, including a copy of the Conservation District\'s written approval letter, shall accompany the Applicant\'s submission of the final stormwater management plan to the Township Engineer. The Township Engineer shall not accept for review any stormwater management plan that does not include evidence of Conservation District approval.

**Condition 12 --- BESS Setbacks.** All battery energy storage system (BESS) components, including battery enclosures, thermal management systems, and associated electrical equipment, shall maintain the following minimum setbacks:

> \(a\) Three hundred (300) feet from any non-participating property line;
>
> \(b\) One thousand (1,000) feet from any occupied dwelling located on a non-participating parcel.

All BESS components shall comply with NFPA 855 (Standard for the Installation of Stationary Energy Storage Systems), as adopted and amended, and all applicable state and local fire codes. Prior to installation of the BESS, the Applicant shall submit BESS design plans and specifications to the Township and the local fire marshal for review and comment.

**Condition 13 --- NPDES and E&S Requirements.** The Applicant shall obtain a National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) General Permit for Stormwater Discharges Associated with Construction Activities (PAG-02) and an approved Erosion and Sedimentation (E&S) Control Plan from the Lancaster County Conservation District prior to any land disturbance on the Project site. No grading, clearing, or construction activity shall commence until these permits and approvals are in hand. Copies of the issued NPDES permit and approved E&S Control Plan shall be provided to the Township prior to the start of construction.

**Category C: Infrastructure and Utilities**

**Condition 14 --- Panel Height.** The maximum height of any solar panel at full tilt shall not exceed twenty (20) feet above finished grade, as measured from the highest point of the panel to the adjacent ground surface at the base of the support structure.

**Condition 15 --- Perimeter Fencing.** The Applicant shall install perimeter security fencing of at least seven (7) feet in height around the entire fenced project area, encompassing approximately 720 acres. The fencing shall include wildlife passage openings, with dimensions of not less than six (6) inches in height and twelve (12) inches in width, at intervals of no more than five hundred (500) feet along the fence line. Fencing design, materials, and proposed locations of wildlife passage openings shall be submitted to the Township Engineer for review and approval prior to installation. All fencing shall be maintained in good condition for the life of the Project.

**Condition 16 --- Vegetative Screening Buffer.** The Applicant shall install a Type C vegetative screening buffer along the northern and eastern project boundaries, at locations adjacent to non-participating properties with occupied residences. The vegetative screening buffer shall meet the following requirements:

> \(a\) The screening buffer shall consist of a mix of native evergreen and deciduous species selected from a list approved by the Township or, in the absence of a Township-approved list, species commonly accepted for screening purposes in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania;
>
> \(b\) The minimum planting height of all screening plantings at the time of installation shall be four (4) feet;
>
> \(c\) The expected mature height of the screening plantings shall be twelve (12) to fifteen (15) feet, sufficient to provide visual screening of the solar panel arrays from adjacent occupied residences;
>
> \(d\) The Applicant shall maintain the vegetative screening buffer for the life of the Project, including regular inspection, watering during establishment, and replacement of any dead, diseased, or damaged plantings within one (1) growing season of identification.

A detailed screening plan, including species selections, spacing, planting methodology, and a maintenance protocol, shall be submitted to the Township for review and approval.

**Condition 17 --- Lighting.** All exterior lighting at the facility shall be downward-directed, fully shielded, and designed to minimize light trespass and sky glow. Lighting shall not exceed 0.5 foot-candles at any property line of the Project site. No continuous nighttime illumination of the solar panel arrays is permitted. Motion-activated security lighting is permitted at substations, inverter pads, operations and maintenance buildings, and access gates, provided such lighting is downward-directed and shielded.

**Condition 18 --- Noise.** Operational noise from the facility, including but not limited to noise generated by solar tracking systems, inverters, transformers, and BESS thermal management systems, shall not exceed forty-five (45) dBA at the nearest non-participating property line, as measured in accordance with ANSI S12.9-2013, Part 3. The Applicant shall, upon written request by the Township, retain a qualified acoustical engineer, at the Applicant\'s sole expense, to conduct noise compliance measurements at the property line locations specified by the Township. Noise compliance measurements shall be conducted within sixty (60) days of the Township\'s written request. Noise from construction activities shall comply with all applicable provisions of the Conestoga Township Noise Ordinance.

**Condition 19 --- Glare Study.** Prior to issuance of building permits for the solar panel installations, the Applicant shall complete and submit to the Township Engineer a solar glare analysis demonstrating no significant glare impact on any public roadway or occupied residence within one (1) mile of the Project boundary. The solar glare analysis shall be prepared by a qualified professional with demonstrated experience in solar glare assessment and shall account for the single-axis tracking configuration proposed for the Project. The analysis shall be submitted in written report form with sufficient detail to allow review by the Township Engineer.

**Condition 20 --- FAA Determination.** In the event that any project structure, including but not limited to meteorological towers, substations, or communications infrastructure, exceeds two hundred (200) feet above ground level (AGL), the Applicant shall obtain a Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Determination of No Hazard to Air Navigation under 14 CFR Part 77 prior to construction of such structure. Evidence of the FAA determination shall be submitted to the Township prior to construction.

**Category D: Financial Assurances**

**Condition 21 --- Decommissioning Plan.** The Applicant shall maintain a Decommissioning Plan for the entire operational life of the Project, from the date of commercial operation through completion of site restoration. The Decommissioning Plan shall provide for the complete removal of all above-ground and below-ground project infrastructure, including solar panels, tracker systems, inverters, substations, fencing, foundations, cabling, and access roads, to a depth of thirty-six (36) inches below finished grade, and the restoration of the Project site to a condition suitable for agricultural use, within eighteen (18) months of the cessation of operations. The initial Decommissioning Plan and Cost Estimate submitted with the Application, as prepared by Ridgepoint Environmental Consultants LLC, is hereby approved as the baseline Decommissioning Plan, subject to updates as required by Condition 23.

**Condition 22 --- Decommissioning Security.** The Applicant shall post decommissioning security in the amount of one hundred twenty-five percent (125%) of the estimated net decommissioning cost. Based upon the current estimated gross decommissioning cost of \$8,400,000, an estimated salvage value of \$2,100,000, and a resulting estimated net decommissioning cost of \$6,300,000, the required decommissioning security is \$7,875,000 (i.e., \$6,300,000 multiplied by 1.25). The decommissioning security shall be posted prior to issuance of the first building permit for the Project. Acceptable forms of decommissioning security include: (a) a surety bond from a surety company authorized to transact business in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania; (b) an irrevocable letter of credit issued by a financial institution rated A- or better by Standard & Poor\'s, Moody\'s, or Fitch; or (c) an escrow account held at a financial institution meeting the same rating requirement. The form and sufficiency of the decommissioning security shall be subject to review and approval by the Township Solicitor.

**Condition 23 --- Decommissioning Cost Estimate Updates.** The Decommissioning Plan and Cost Estimate shall be updated every five (5) years from the date of commercial operation by a licensed professional engineer retained by the Applicant, at the Applicant\'s expense. Each updated cost estimate shall reflect then-current costs of labor, equipment, transportation, and disposal, as well as any changes in salvage value. If the updated net decommissioning cost estimate exceeds the amount secured by the existing decommissioning security, the Applicant shall increase the decommissioning security to one hundred twenty-five percent (125%) of the updated net cost within ninety (90) days of receipt of the updated estimate by the Township. The updated cost estimate shall be submitted to the Township Engineer for review.

**Condition 24 --- Decommissioning Trigger.** If the facility ceases to generate and export electricity to the grid for a continuous period of twelve (12) months, and such cessation is not attributable to force majeure or a planned maintenance or repowering program approved by the Township, the Township may declare the facility abandoned by written notice to the Applicant. Following receipt of such notice, the Applicant shall have ninety (90) days to contest the declaration by providing the Township with credible evidence of planned resumption of operations within a reasonable timeframe. If the Applicant fails to contest the declaration or fails to provide satisfactory evidence of planned resumption, the Township may draw upon the decommissioning security and proceed with decommissioning in accordance with the approved Decommissioning Plan.

**Condition 25 --- Road Maintenance Bond.** The Applicant shall post a road maintenance bond in the amount of Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000) prior to commencement of construction activities. The road maintenance bond shall secure the Applicant\'s obligation to repair any damage to Township roads attributable to Project construction traffic. Upon completion of construction and acceptance of road repairs by the Township Engineer, the road maintenance bond shall be reduced to One Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$150,000) for the operational period of the facility, to address potential road impacts from ongoing maintenance and operational vehicle traffic. The bond shall be in a form acceptable to the Township Solicitor and shall remain in effect for the duration of the Project\'s operational life.

**Condition 26 --- Road Improvement Requirements.** The Applicant shall, at its sole expense, engage a qualified engineering firm to perform pre-construction and post-construction road condition surveys on all Township roads within one (1) mile of the primary construction access point on Hershey Mill Road. The pre-construction survey shall be completed and submitted to the Township Engineer prior to commencement of construction activities. The post-construction survey shall be completed and submitted within sixty (60) days of substantial completion of construction. Any deterioration of Township road surfaces, drainage structures, or related infrastructure attributable to Project construction traffic, as determined by the Township Engineer, shall be repaired by the Applicant to the satisfaction of the Township Engineer within six (6) months of the completion of construction.

**Condition 27 --- Construction Traffic Plan.** A construction traffic management plan shall be prepared by a qualified traffic engineer and submitted to the Township Engineer for review and approval at least sixty (60) days prior to commencement of construction activities. The plan shall specify designated haul routes, traffic control measures, flagging procedures, hours of construction vehicle operations, load limits, and any temporary road closures or detours required during construction. Construction vehicle operations on Township roads shall be limited to the hours of 7:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday through Saturday, unless otherwise approved by the Township.

**Condition 28 --- Agricultural Mitigation Payment.** The Applicant shall make an agricultural mitigation payment to Lancaster Farmland Trust in the amount of Seven Hundred Forty-Seven Thousand Six Hundred Dollars (\$747,600), calculated as 620 acres of prime agricultural land at \$1,200 per acre. Payment shall be made in full prior to issuance of the first building permit for the Project. Evidence of payment, including a receipt or acknowledgment letter from Lancaster Farmland Trust, shall be submitted to the Township.

**Condition 29 --- School District Taxes.** The Applicant shall pay all applicable school district real estate taxes assessed against the Project parcels in accordance with applicable law. The Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) agreement between the Applicant and the Township does not apply to or affect the Applicant\'s obligation to pay school district taxes.

**Condition 30 --- PILOT Agreement.** Prior to issuance of any building permit for the Project, the Applicant and the Township shall execute a Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) Agreement in a form satisfactory to the Township Solicitor, reflecting the negotiated terms of Three Hundred Eighty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$385,000) per year for Years 1 through 15 of commercial operation, with a two percent (2%) annual escalator commencing thereafter for the remaining term of the agreement. As of the date of this Decision, the formal PILOT Agreement has not yet been executed. The issuance of building permits for the Project is expressly conditioned upon execution of the PILOT Agreement by both parties.

**Category E: Operations and Maintenance**

**Condition 31 --- Maintenance Obligations.** The Applicant shall maintain all Project components, including solar panels, tracker systems, inverters, substations, battery storage units, perimeter fencing, vegetative screening buffers, access roads, and stormwater management facilities, in good working order and in compliance with all conditions of this Decision for the entire operational life of the Project. Any component that fails, is damaged, or deteriorates to a condition that creates a safety hazard or violates the terms of this Decision shall be repaired or replaced within a reasonable time, not to exceed ninety (90) days, unless a longer period is approved by the Township Engineer.

**Condition 32 --- Annual Reporting.** The Applicant shall provide an annual compliance report to the Board of Supervisors of Conestoga Township, on or before March 31 of each year, summarizing facility operations, electricity generation, maintenance activities performed during the prior calendar year, the status and adequacy of all financial assurances, and the Applicant\'s compliance with all conditions of this Decision during the prior calendar year. The first annual report shall be due on March 31 of the first full calendar year following the date of commercial operation.

**Condition 33 --- Emergency Response Plan.** The Applicant shall prepare and submit a comprehensive Emergency Response Plan to the Township, the Conestoga Township Volunteer Fire Company, and the Lancaster County Emergency Management Agency not less than thirty (30) days prior to commencement of commercial operations. The Emergency Response Plan shall address emergency procedures for all components of the Project, including but not limited to electrical emergencies, fire, severe weather events, and natural disasters. For the battery energy storage system, the Emergency Response Plan shall specifically and in detail address thermal runaway scenarios, fire suppression protocols and equipment, hazardous material containment and spill response, emergency notification procedures, and evacuation protocols for personnel and nearby residents. The Applicant shall conduct at least one tabletop emergency exercise with the local fire department and emergency management personnel within six (6) months of the commencement of commercial operations and annually thereafter.

**Category F: General and Administrative**

**Condition 34 --- Timing of Financial Assurances.** All financial assurances required under this Decision and Order, including the decommissioning security required by Condition 22, the road maintenance bond required by Condition 25, and the agricultural mitigation payment required by Condition 28, shall be in place no later than sixty (60) days prior to the commencement of construction activities. Evidence of compliance with this condition shall be submitted to the Township Solicitor and the Township Engineer in writing.

**Condition 35 --- Modification and Amendment.** Any material modification to the approved Site Plan or project design, including but not limited to changes in total project acreage, panel height, setbacks, BESS capacity, or interconnection configuration, shall require submission of an amended Conditional Use Application and compliance with all notice and hearing requirements of the MPC and the Ordinance. Notwithstanding the foregoing, modifications that do not constitute material changes may, at the discretion of the Board of Supervisors, be approved administratively upon written certification by the Township Engineer that the modification does not increase the impact of the Project on adjacent properties beyond that contemplated by this Decision. Minor field adjustments that do not alter setbacks, height, total project acreage, or the number of project parcels may be approved in writing by the Township Engineer without further action by the Board.

**[VII. DISSENTING OPINION SUMMARY]{.underline}**

The conditional use approval was granted by a vote of three (3) to two (2). Supervisor Karen Beiler and Supervisor Jonas Lapp voted against the approval of the Conditional Use Application and dissented from this Decision and Order.

The dissenting Supervisors expressed their objections to the approval on the following grounds:

First, Supervisors Beiler and Lapp stated their belief that a utility-scale solar energy facility of this magnitude --- encompassing 850 acres and converting approximately 623 acres of prime agricultural land from active farm use --- is fundamentally incompatible with the agricultural character of the Agricultural-Rural (A-R) zoning district. The dissenting members expressed the view that the 2023 amendment to the Ordinance permitting solar energy systems as a conditional use in the A-R district was not intended to authorize projects of this scale, and that the approval sets a concerning precedent for future large-scale development in the Township\'s agricultural areas.

Second, Supervisors Beiler and Lapp expressed concern that the long-term impacts of the Project on property values of adjacent non-participating properties have not been fully or adequately addressed by the property value impact assessment prepared by the Clarendon Appraisal Group. The dissenting members noted that the Clarendon report relies heavily on comparable data from other regions and that local market conditions and community character in Conestoga Township may not be fully captured by the available empirical studies.

Third, the dissenting members stated their belief that the conditions imposed in this Decision, while extensive, are insufficient to fully mitigate the visual, environmental, and quality-of-life impacts of the Project on neighboring properties. Supervisors Beiler and Lapp specifically cited concerns about the adequacy of screening buffers, the potential long-term environmental effects of the battery energy storage system, and the disruption to the rural landscape character of the Township.

The dissent is noted for the record. This Decision and Order reflects the majority action of the Board.

**[VIII. SIGNATURE BLOCK]{.underline}**

**[CONESTOGA TOWNSHIP ZONING ORDINANCE]{.underline}**

**[Chapter 27 --- Zoning]{.underline}**

**Lancaster County, Pennsylvania**

**Section 27-605(B)(14): Utility-Scale Solar Energy Systems** **Conditional Use in the Agricultural-Rural (A-R) Zoning District**

*As amended by Ordinance No. 2023-12, adopted December 18, 2023, effective December 28, 2023.*

This document is an excerpt from the Conestoga Township Zoning Ordinance, Chapter 27, and is provided for reference purposes only. The complete Zoning Ordinance is available for inspection at the Conestoga Township offices, 1220 Millwood Road, Conestoga, Pennsylvania 17516, and on the Township website at www.conestogatwp.org. In the event of any discrepancy between this excerpt and the official codified ordinance on file with the Township Secretary, the official codified ordinance shall control.

**[Section 27-601. Purpose and Intent]{.underline}**

Conditional uses are those land uses which, due to their particular characteristics, may be appropriate in certain zoning districts but which require individual review and approval by the Board of Supervisors to ensure compatibility with surrounding properties, consistency with the goals and objectives of the Conestoga Township Comprehensive Plan, and compliance with the general and specific standards set forth in this Article VI. The Board of Supervisors shall grant a conditional use application only upon a finding that the applicant has satisfied all applicable general standards of Section 27-602 and the specific standards applicable to the proposed use as set forth in Section 27-605. The authority of the Board of Supervisors to review and approve conditional uses is conferred by the Pennsylvania Municipalities Planning Code (MPC), 53 P.S. §§ 10101 *et seq.*, and in particular Article VI thereof, and shall be exercised in accordance with the substantive and procedural requirements of the MPC and this Ordinance.

**[Section 27-602. General Standards for All Conditional Uses]{.underline}**

In addition to the specific standards applicable to each individual conditional use as set forth in Section 27-605, all conditional use applications shall be evaluated against the following general standards. No conditional use shall be approved unless the Board of Supervisors finds that the applicant has demonstrated compliance with each of the following:

> \(a\) The proposed use shall not be detrimental to the health, safety, and welfare of the residents of the Township and the surrounding community.
>
> \(b\) The proposed use shall be consistent with the goals, objectives, and policies of the Conestoga Township Comprehensive Plan, as adopted and amended from time to time.
>
> \(c\) The proposed use shall not adversely affect the character, property values, or orderly development of the surrounding neighborhood or zoning district in which the use is proposed to be located.
>
> \(d\) Adequate public infrastructure, including but not limited to roads, stormwater management facilities, water supply, and sewage disposal, exists or will be provided by the applicant to serve the proposed use in a manner that does not place an undue burden on the Township or its residents.
>
> \(e\) The applicant has demonstrated compliance with all other applicable Township, county, state, and federal regulations, including but not limited to stormwater management, erosion and sedimentation control, floodplain management, wetland protection, and historic preservation requirements.

These general standards shall apply in addition to, and not in lieu of, the specific standards applicable to each conditional use category as set forth in Section 27-605 of this Ordinance.

**[Section 27-605. Conditional Uses in the Agricultural-Rural (A-R) District]{.underline}**

**Section 27-605(A). Permitted Conditional Uses**

The following land uses may be permitted as conditional uses in the Agricultural-Rural (A-R) Zoning District, subject to the applicable general standards of Section 27-602 and the specific standards set forth in Section 27-605(B) for each use category:

> (B)(1) Public and private schools.
>
> (B)(2) Places of worship and religious institutions.
>
> (B)(3) Cemeteries and memorial gardens.
>
> (B)(4) Agricultural commercial enterprises.
>
> (B)(5) Communication towers and wireless telecommunications facilities.
>
> (B)(6) Bed-and-breakfast establishments.
>
> (B)(7) Rural event venues.
>
> (B)(8) Veterinary clinics and animal hospitals.
>
> (B)(9) Farm-based composting facilities.
>
> (B)(10) Wind energy systems.
>
> (B)(11) Mineral extraction and quarrying operations.
>
> (B)(12) Outdoor recreation facilities.
>
> (B)(13) Intensive agricultural operations.
>
> **(B)(14) Utility-scale solar energy systems.**
>
> **(B)(15) Energy storage facilities.**
>
> (B)(16) Agritourism operations.

Each conditional use category listed above is subject to separate and distinct specific standards as set forth in the corresponding subsection of Section 27-605(B). Where a proposed development includes components that fall within more than one conditional use category, the applicant shall demonstrate compliance with the specific standards applicable to each category, unless this Ordinance expressly provides otherwise.

**[Section 27-605(B)(14). Utility-Scale Solar Energy Systems --- Conditional Use Standards]{.underline}**

**Section 27-605(B)(14)(a). Definitions**

For the purposes of this Section 27-605(B)(14), the following terms shall have the meanings ascribed to them herein. Where a term defined in this subsection conflicts with a definition of the same term in Section 27-210 of this Ordinance, the definition in this subsection shall control for the purposes of interpreting and applying the provisions of this Section 27-605(B)(14).

**\"Utility-Scale Solar Energy System\"** --- A solar photovoltaic energy generation facility with a nameplate alternating current (AC) capacity exceeding ten (10) megawatts (MW), including all associated solar panels, racking systems, inverters, transformers, power conversion stations, electrical collection systems, access roads, and related infrastructure located on the project site. The term \"utility-scale solar energy system\" shall not include small-scale or community solar energy systems with a nameplate AC capacity of ten (10) megawatts or less, which are subject to separate provisions of this Ordinance.

**\"Project Site\"** --- The contiguous or non-contiguous parcels of land upon which the utility-scale solar energy system and its associated infrastructure are proposed to be constructed, installed, and operated, as depicted on the approved site plan submitted as part of the conditional use application. The project site shall include all parcels identified in the application as hosting solar panels, racking systems, inverters, substations, energy storage facilities, internal access roads, stormwater management facilities, and vegetative screening buffers. The project site shall not include off-site linear infrastructure such as transmission lines, generation tie lines, access roads located outside the project boundary, or utility interconnection facilities not located on the parcels identified in the conditional use application.

**\"Energy Storage Facility\"** --- A system designed to store electrical energy, including but not limited to battery energy storage systems (BESS), flywheel energy storage, compressed air energy storage, and other technologies, for later injection into the electrical grid or for use by the generation facility, with a storage capacity exceeding five (5) megawatt-hours (MWh). An energy storage facility may be approved as a standalone conditional use under Section 27-605(B)(15) of this Ordinance or as an accessory or secondary use to a utility-scale solar energy system under this Section 27-605(B)(14), provided that all dimensional and performance standards applicable to energy storage facilities under Section 27-605(B)(15) are also met when the energy storage facility is associated with a utility-scale solar energy system.

**\"Non-Participating Property\"** --- Any lot or parcel of land, as recorded in the office of the Lancaster County Recorder of Deeds, that is not subject to a lease, easement, option, or other written agreement with the applicant or the applicant\'s affiliates, successors, or assigns for the purpose of hosting, supporting, or otherwise facilitating the construction, installation, or operation of the utility-scale solar energy system or any component thereof.

**\"Non-Participating Property Line\"** --- The property boundary of a non-participating property, as depicted on the recorded deed or subdivision plan for such property.

**\"Occupied Dwelling\"** --- Any building or structure designed for or used as a permanent or seasonal residence that is occupied or capable of occupancy at the time the conditional use application is filed with the Township. A dwelling shall be deemed \"capable of occupancy\" if it is served by water and sewage facilities, is structurally sound, and has not been formally condemned by the Township or other governmental authority.

**\"Decommissioning\"** --- The removal of all above-ground and below-ground components of a utility-scale solar energy system, including but not limited to solar panels, racking systems, inverters, transformers, substations, energy storage equipment, fencing, access roads, and foundations, the restoration of the project site to substantially its pre-construction condition suitable for the prior use of the land, and the recycling or proper disposal of all removed materials in accordance with applicable state and federal law, upon the cessation of operations.

**\"Solar Glare\"** --- The reflection of sunlight from solar panels, racking systems, or related surfaces toward an observer, including reflected light that is visible from public roadways, occupied dwellings on non-participating properties, and aircraft flight paths, and that may create a hazard or nuisance.

**\"Type C Vegetative Screening Buffer\"** --- A landscaped buffer area consisting of a mix of native evergreen and deciduous trees and shrubs, planted at intervals and densities sufficient to provide a year-round visual screen of at least seventy-five percent (75%) opacity within five (5) years of planting, as further specified in Section 27-605(B)(14)(d) of this Ordinance.

**\"Gen-Tie Line\" or \"Generation Tie Line\"** --- An electrical transmission line connecting a generation facility, such as a utility-scale solar energy system, to the point of interconnection with the regional transmission system or an existing electrical substation operated by the local electric distribution company or regional transmission operator. A gen-tie line is not considered part of the utility-scale solar energy system or the project site for purposes of this Section 27-605(B)(14).

**Section 27-605(B)(14)(b). Application Requirements**

An applicant seeking conditional use approval for a utility-scale solar energy system under this Section shall submit the following materials to the Township Zoning Officer as part of a complete conditional use application:

> \(1\) A completed conditional use application form, as adopted by the Board of Supervisors, signed by the applicant or its authorized representative, and accompanied by the application fee established by resolution of the Board of Supervisors.
>
> \(2\) A site plan, prepared and sealed by a licensed professional engineer or licensed surveyor registered in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, drawn to a scale no smaller than 1 inch = 100 feet, depicting: (i) all parcel boundaries comprising the project site, with tax parcel identification numbers; (ii) the proposed locations of all solar panels, racking systems, inverters, power conversion stations, substations, energy storage facilities, internal collection lines, access roads, fencing, gates, and other infrastructure; (iii) all applicable setback lines as required by Section 27-605(B)(14)(c); (iv) all existing structures, including occupied dwellings, within one thousand (1,000) feet of the project site boundary; (v) proposed vegetative screening buffer locations and landscaping; (vi) existing topography at two-foot contour intervals; and (vii) proposed grading and finished elevations.
>
> \(3\) A narrative description of the proposed technology, including solar panel type and manufacturer, racking system design (fixed-tilt or single-axis tracker), inverter specifications and locations, transformer and substation design, and the nameplate generation capacity of the facility in both alternating current (AC) and direct current (DC) megawatts.
>
> \(4\) Evidence of site control, in the form of executed leases, options to lease, easements, or proof of fee ownership, for all parcels comprising the project site.
>
> \(5\) A preliminary stormwater management plan prepared in accordance with the Conestoga Township Stormwater Management Ordinance, Chapter 26, and the Lancaster County Act 167 Stormwater Management Plan, demonstrating compliance with all applicable stormwater management requirements.
>
> \(6\) A preliminary erosion and sedimentation control plan prepared in accordance with the regulations of the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection and the Lancaster County Conservation District.
>
> \(7\) A noise impact assessment prepared by a qualified acoustical engineer, modeling the anticipated noise levels from all components of the utility-scale solar energy system at the nearest non-participating property lines and nearest occupied dwellings on non-participating properties.
>
> \(8\) A solar glare analysis evaluating the potential for solar glare from the proposed facility to affect occupied dwellings on non-participating properties, public roadways, and known aircraft flight paths in the vicinity of the project site.
>
> \(9\) A decommissioning plan and cost estimate prepared by a licensed professional engineer registered in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, in accordance with Section 27-605(B)(14)(i).
>
> \(10\) Evidence of consultation with the Pennsylvania Natural Diversity Inventory (PNDI) program, including the initial PNDI screening results, and copies of any required follow-up correspondence with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, the Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission, and/or the Pennsylvania Game Commission.
>
> \(11\) A cultural resources assessment, prepared by a qualified professional meeting the Secretary of the Interior\'s Professional Qualification Standards, if the project site or any portion thereof is within two hundred (200) feet of a known or potentially eligible historic resource listed in or eligible for listing in the National Register of Historic Places, or if such assessment is required by the Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission (PHMC).
>
> \(12\) A property value impact assessment, if requested by the Board of Supervisors at or prior to the first hearing on the conditional use application, to be prepared by a state-certified general appraiser retained by the Township at the applicant\'s expense.
>
> \(13\) A traffic impact study addressing both construction-phase and operational-phase vehicle trips, prepared in accordance with PennDOT requirements and the standards of the Institute of Transportation Engineers (ITE).
>
> \(14\) Proof of application to the applicable regional transmission organization for electrical interconnection of the proposed facility.
>
> \(15\) An advisory review letter from the Lancaster County Planning Commission, as required by Section 609 of the Pennsylvania Municipalities Planning Code, 53 P.S. § 10609.
>
> \(16\) Such additional information as the Board of Supervisors may reasonably request to evaluate the conditional use application and ensure compliance with the standards of this Ordinance.

An application shall not be deemed complete for purposes of scheduling a public hearing until all items listed above have been submitted to the Township Zoning Officer. The Zoning Officer shall notify the applicant in writing within thirty (30) days of submission if any items are missing or incomplete.

Where an energy storage facility is proposed as an accessory or secondary use to a utility-scale solar energy system, the dimensional standards for energy storage facilities under Section 27-605(B)(15)(c) shall also apply to such energy storage components.
