**Section 27-605(B)(14)(d). Screening and Landscaping**

The following screening and landscaping standards shall apply to all utility-scale solar energy systems:

> \(1\) A Type C vegetative screening buffer, as defined in Section 27-605(B)(14)(a), shall be installed along any project site boundary that is adjacent to: (i) a non-participating property containing an occupied dwelling located within one thousand (1,000) feet of the project site boundary; or (ii) a public road right-of-way.
>
> \(2\) The vegetative screening buffer shall be a minimum of thirty (30) feet in width, measured perpendicular to the project site boundary, and shall be located entirely within the project site boundary.
>
> \(3\) The buffer shall consist of a mix of native evergreen and deciduous trees and shrubs, planted at densities and intervals sufficient to achieve the opacity standard specified in subsection (4) below. A minimum of sixty percent (60%) of the plantings shall be evergreen species to ensure year-round screening effectiveness.
>
> \(4\) All plantings shall be a minimum of four (4) feet in height at the time of installation and shall achieve a minimum mature height of twelve (12) to fifteen (15) feet. The buffer shall achieve a minimum of seventy-five percent (75%) visual opacity within five (5) years of planting, as determined by the Township Engineer or a qualified landscape architect retained by the Township.
>
> \(5\) The applicant shall submit a landscaping plan prepared by a licensed landscape architect registered in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, identifying species, spacing, projected growth rates, and a maintenance schedule. The landscaping plan shall be submitted as part of the conditional use application and shall be subject to review and approval by the Board of Supervisors.
>
> \(6\) All plantings shall consist of species native to southeastern Pennsylvania, as identified by the Pennsylvania Department of Conservation and Natural Resources or an equivalent authoritative source. Invasive species, as listed on the Pennsylvania Department of Agriculture\'s Noxious Weed Control List, shall not be used.
>
> \(7\) The applicant shall be responsible for the ongoing maintenance, irrigation (if necessary to establish plantings), and replacement of any dead, diseased, or damaged plantings for the operational life of the facility. Any planting that fails to survive shall be replaced with a plant of the same or comparable species and minimum size within the next planting season following discovery of the loss.
>
> \(8\) Existing mature vegetation, hedgerows, and tree lines within the buffer area may be credited toward compliance with the screening requirements of this subsection if the Township Engineer or a qualified landscape architect retained by the Township determines that such existing vegetation provides visual screening equivalent to or exceeding the standards set forth herein.

**Section 27-605(B)(14)(e). Perimeter Fencing and Security**

The following fencing and security standards shall apply to all utility-scale solar energy systems:

> \(1\) The entire project area containing solar panels, energy storage facilities, inverters, substations, power conversion stations, and related electrical equipment shall be enclosed by security fencing. The security fence shall define a continuous and secure perimeter around all energized and potentially hazardous components of the facility.
>
> \(2\) Fencing shall be a minimum of seven (7) feet in height and shall be constructed of durable, weather-resistant materials. Fencing shall be topped with angled extension arms or similar deterrent devices to discourage unauthorized entry. The use of barbed wire, razor wire, or electrified fencing is expressly prohibited.
>
> \(3\) Wildlife passage openings shall be incorporated into the perimeter fence at intervals of no more than five hundred (500) feet along the total perimeter length to allow passage of small mammals, reptiles, and other ground-dwelling wildlife. Each wildlife passage opening shall be a minimum of six (6) inches in height and twelve (12) inches in width at ground level, and shall be designed to prevent unauthorized human entry while permitting wildlife movement.
>
> \(4\) All fencing shall be set back a minimum of ten (10) feet from the interior edge of any vegetative screening buffer to allow adequate access for buffer maintenance, including mowing, pruning, irrigation, and replanting activities.
>
> \(5\) Vehicular access gates shall be provided at each designated access point to the project site and shall be designed and constructed to accommodate emergency vehicle access. All gates shall remain locked when the facility is unattended and shall be equipped with a lock box or similar device providing emergency responders with rapid access.
>
> \(6\) Warning signage reading \"No Trespassing\" and \"Danger --- High Voltage\" shall be posted at intervals of no more than two hundred fifty (250) feet along the perimeter fence and at all gates. Signage shall be weather-resistant, legible at a distance of at least twenty-five (25) feet, and shall comply with applicable OSHA and National Electrical Code standards.

**Section 27-605(B)(14)(f). Environmental and Natural Resource Protection**

> \(1\) **Stormwater Management.** The applicant shall comply with all applicable stormwater management requirements of the Conestoga Township Stormwater Management Ordinance, Chapter 26, and the Lancaster County Act 167 Stormwater Management Plan. A final stormwater management plan, prepared and sealed by a licensed professional engineer registered in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, shall be submitted to and approved by the Township Engineer prior to the issuance of any building permit or grading permit. The stormwater management plan shall first be reviewed and approved by the Lancaster County Conservation District. The plan shall address both the construction phase and the operational phase of the facility, including the effects of impervious and semi-impervious surfaces (such as solar panels and access roads) on stormwater runoff volumes, peak flow rates, and water quality. The applicant shall demonstrate that post-development stormwater runoff will not exceed pre-development conditions for the two-year, ten-year, twenty-five-year, fifty-year, and one-hundred-year design storm events.
>
> \(2\) **Erosion and Sediment Control.** The applicant shall obtain all required NPDES General Permits for Stormwater Discharges Associated with Construction Activities (PAG-02) from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection and shall prepare and implement an Erosion and Sedimentation (E&S) Control Plan approved by the Lancaster County Conservation District prior to any land disturbance activity on the project site. The E&S Control Plan shall be prepared in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 102 and the standards of the Lancaster County Conservation District.
>
> \(3\) **Threatened and Endangered Species.** The applicant shall complete a Pennsylvania Natural Diversity Inventory (PNDI) environmental review for the entire project site and shall comply with all required consultations with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, the Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission, and/or the Pennsylvania Game Commission regarding potential impacts to federal or state-listed threatened and endangered species. All necessary consultations shall be completed and all required clearance letters or determinations shall be obtained prior to any land disturbance activity on the affected parcels. The applicant shall implement all avoidance, minimization, and mitigation measures identified through the consultation process.
>
> \(4\) **Cultural and Historic Resources.** If the project site or any portion thereof is located within two hundred (200) feet of a known or potentially eligible historic resource listed in or eligible for listing in the National Register of Historic Places, or if the project involves a federal action or federal funding triggering review under Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act, the applicant shall complete consultation with the Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission (PHMC) in accordance with applicable state and federal laws, including the Pennsylvania History Code, 37 Pa. C.S. §§ 101 *et seq.* The applicant shall not commence grading, excavation, or other earth-disturbing activities in the vicinity of any such resource until the PHMC has issued a written determination regarding the project\'s potential effect on the resource and any required mitigation measures have been agreed upon.
>
> \(5\) **Wetlands and Watercourses.** No solar panels, energy storage facilities, permanent access roads, or permanent structures shall be located within any wetland, jurisdictional watercourse, floodplain, or riparian buffer area as defined and delineated in accordance with applicable federal regulations (including Section 404 of the Clean Water Act and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Wetland Delineation Manual), applicable state regulations, and the Conestoga Township Floodplain Management Ordinance. The applicant shall provide a wetland delineation and a floodplain analysis prepared by qualified professionals as part of the conditional use application if any portion of the project site is identified as potentially containing wetlands or floodplain areas.
>
> \(6\) **Agricultural Mitigation.** For any utility-scale solar energy system located on land classified as prime agricultural land, as defined by the U.S. Department of Agriculture, Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS), including soils classified as \"prime farmland\" or \"farmland of statewide importance,\" the applicant shall make a one-time agricultural mitigation payment to a qualified agricultural land conservation organization approved by the Board of Supervisors. The mitigation payment shall be calculated at a rate of one thousand two hundred dollars (\$1,200.00) per acre of prime agricultural land converted from active agricultural use as a result of the construction and operation of the solar energy system. The total acreage subject to the mitigation payment shall be the acreage within the project site that is classified as prime farmland or farmland of statewide importance, as verified by the NRCS soil survey data and confirmed by the Lancaster County Conservation District. The payment shall be made in full prior to the issuance of any building permit or grading permit for the project.

**Section 27-605(B)(14)(g). Performance Standards**

All utility-scale solar energy systems shall comply with the following performance standards during both construction and operation:

> \(1\) **Noise.** Operational noise generated by a utility-scale solar energy system, including but not limited to noise from inverters, transformers, power conversion stations, tracking motors, and energy storage system cooling equipment, shall not exceed forty-five (45) dBA as measured at the nearest non-participating property line. Noise measurements shall be conducted in accordance with applicable ANSI standards for environmental sound measurement. The noise impact assessment required by Section 27-605(B)(14)(b)(7) shall model noise levels under worst-case operating conditions and shall identify any mitigation measures necessary to achieve compliance with the forty-five (45) dBA standard. Construction-phase noise shall be exempt from this standard but shall comply with applicable Township noise regulations and the hours-of-construction limitations imposed by the Board of Supervisors as a condition of approval.
>
> \(2\) **Solar Glare.** The applicant shall demonstrate through a solar glare analysis that the utility-scale solar energy system will not produce solar glare that creates a significant hazard or nuisance to occupants of nearby occupied dwellings on non-participating properties, users of public roadways, or aircraft operating in the vicinity of the project site. A solar glare analysis shall be submitted with the conditional use application as required by Section 27-605(B)(14)(b)(8). Where solar glare impacts are identified, the applicant shall propose mitigation measures such as panel orientation adjustments, anti-reflective coatings, or vegetative screening to eliminate or minimize the identified impacts to the satisfaction of the Board of Supervisors.
>
> \(3\) **Electromagnetic Interference.** The utility-scale solar energy system shall not cause interference with radio, television, telephone, cellular, emergency communication, or other communication signals to neighboring properties or public facilities. The applicant shall promptly investigate and resolve any documented interference complaints within thirty (30) days of receiving written notice from the Township or an affected property owner.
>
> \(4\) **Lighting.** All on-site lighting shall be shielded and directed downward to minimize light pollution and shall not cause illumination to be cast upon any adjacent property or public roadway in excess of 0.5 foot-candles measured at the property line. Lighting shall be limited to the minimum necessary for safety and security purposes and shall comply with the Township\'s outdoor lighting standards set forth in Chapter 27, Section 27-710 of this Ordinance. Security lighting at substations, energy storage facilities, and access gates may be equipped with motion-activated sensors to reduce continuous nighttime lighting.
>
> \(5\) **Dust and Erosion.** During construction, the applicant shall implement dust suppression measures, including but not limited to watering of access roads and exposed soil areas, application of dust suppressants, and stabilization of stockpiled materials, to minimize airborne particulate matter. All disturbed areas not covered by solar panels, equipment, access roads, or hardscaping shall be stabilized with permanent vegetation or approved ground cover within thirty (30) days of final grading of each phase of construction. Seed mixes used for ground cover shall consist of native grasses and pollinator-friendly species appropriate for southeastern Pennsylvania.

**Section 27-605(B)(14)(h). Access and Transportation**

> \(1\) The applicant shall provide a traffic impact study addressing construction-phase traffic, including the delivery of oversized and overweight equipment, solar panels, racking systems, energy storage components, and aggregate materials, and operational-phase traffic, including routine maintenance vehicle trips and periodic equipment replacement activities. The traffic impact study shall be prepared in accordance with PennDOT and ITE standards and shall identify the proposed construction vehicle routes, estimated number and type of vehicle trips by construction phase, and proposed mitigation measures for any identified impacts.
>
> \(2\) All construction traffic shall utilize routes approved by the Township Engineer in consultation with PennDOT and the applicable road authority. The applicant shall enter into a road maintenance agreement with the Township, in a form satisfactory to the Township Solicitor, and shall post a road maintenance bond or other acceptable financial security in an amount determined by the Board of Supervisors, based upon the recommendation of the Township Engineer, to ensure the repair of any damage to Township roads caused by construction-related traffic and activities. The road maintenance bond shall be posted prior to the commencement of construction.
>
> \(3\) Access to the project site shall be provided via a minimum of two (2) access points, each with a minimum driveway width of twenty (20) feet, designed and constructed to accommodate emergency vehicle access, including fire apparatus. Access points shall be designed to provide adequate sight distance in accordance with PennDOT standards and shall be approved by the Township Engineer.
>
> \(4\) During the operational phase, the facility shall not generate more than ten (10) vehicle trips per day on average, calculated on a monthly basis, excluding scheduled maintenance events, emergency response activities, and deliveries of replacement equipment. The applicant shall maintain a log of operational vehicle trips and shall make such log available to the Township upon request.

**Section 27-605(B)(14)(i). Decommissioning**

> \(1\) The applicant shall submit a decommissioning plan with the conditional use application describing in detail the process for removal of all above-ground and below-ground components of the utility-scale solar energy system, including solar panels, racking systems, inverters, transformers, substations, energy storage equipment, fencing, access roads, foundations, and underground electrical conduit, and the restoration of the project site to substantially its pre-construction condition suitable for resumption of the prior land use.
>
> \(2\) The applicant shall provide a decommissioning cost estimate prepared and sealed by a licensed professional engineer registered in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, which shall include: (i) the estimated gross cost of decommissioning, including removal of all above-ground and below-ground components to a depth of no less than thirty-six (36) inches below finished grade, site restoration, revegetation, and the proper disposal or recycling of all removed materials in accordance with applicable state and federal waste management regulations; and (ii) the estimated net salvage value of all recoverable materials, supported by current market data for recyclable commodities.
>
> \(3\) Decommissioning security shall be posted by the applicant in an amount equal to one hundred twenty-five percent (125%) of the estimated net decommissioning cost (the gross cost of decommissioning minus the estimated net salvage value of recoverable materials). The net salvage value credit shall not reduce the required security amount to less than seventy-five percent (75%) of the estimated gross decommissioning cost.
>
> \(4\) Acceptable forms of decommissioning security shall include: (i) an irrevocable standby letter of credit issued by a financial institution with a long-term credit rating of A- or better from a nationally recognized statistical rating organization (such as Standard & Poor\'s, Moody\'s, or Fitch), or an equivalent rating from a comparable rating agency; (ii) a surety bond issued by a surety company authorized to do business in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania with an A.M. Best rating of A- VII or better; or (iii) an escrow account held by a financial institution meeting the credit rating requirements of clause (i), with the Township named as a beneficiary. The form and terms of the decommissioning security instrument shall be subject to approval by the Township Solicitor.
>
> \(5\) The decommissioning security shall be posted prior to the issuance of the first building permit for the utility-scale solar energy system. No building permit shall be issued until the Township Solicitor has confirmed that the decommissioning security instrument is in proper form and has been fully executed and delivered.
>
> \(6\) The decommissioning cost estimate shall be updated every five (5) years from the date of commercial operation by a licensed professional engineer registered in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania. Each updated estimate shall be submitted to the Township within thirty (30) days of completion. If the updated estimate results in a net decommissioning cost that exceeds the amount of the existing security, the applicant shall increase the security to one hundred twenty-five percent (125%) of the updated net decommissioning cost within sixty (60) days of the date of the updated estimate. If the updated estimate results in a net decommissioning cost that is less than the existing security amount, the applicant may request a reduction in the security, which shall be approved by the Board of Supervisors upon verification of the updated estimate by the Township Engineer.
>
> \(7\) Decommissioning shall be completed within twelve (12) months of the date on which the facility ceases generating and delivering electricity to the grid for a continuous period of twelve (12) months, unless the applicant demonstrates to the satisfaction of the Board of Supervisors, by clear and convincing evidence, that the cessation of operations is temporary and that the facility will resume generating electricity within a reasonable period not to exceed an additional twelve (12) months. In no event shall the total period of non-generation exceed twenty-four (24) consecutive months without the commencement of decommissioning.
>
> \(8\) If the applicant fails to complete decommissioning within the timeframe required by subsection (7) above, the Township shall provide written notice to the applicant and the issuer of the decommissioning security instrument. If decommissioning is not substantially completed within ninety (90) days of such notice, the Township may draw upon the decommissioning security and utilize the proceeds to complete the decommissioning of the facility at the applicant\'s expense. Any costs incurred by the Township in excess of the security amount shall constitute a lien against the project site parcels in accordance with applicable law.

**Section 27-605(B)(14)(j). Financial Assurances and Fiscal Impact**

> \(1\) The Board of Supervisors may require the applicant to enter into a Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) Agreement with the Township as a condition of conditional use approval if the applicant intends to seek any tax exemption, abatement, alternative energy credit, or alternative assessment for the utility-scale solar energy system under applicable state law, including but not limited to the Alternative Energy Production Tax Credit Act or any other statute that may reduce or eliminate the applicant\'s real property tax liability for the solar energy facility or its components.
>
> \(2\) The terms, duration, and payment amounts of any PILOT agreement shall be negotiated between the applicant and the Township and shall be set forth in a written agreement in a form satisfactory to the Township Solicitor. The PILOT agreement shall be executed and recorded in the office of the Lancaster County Recorder of Deeds prior to the issuance of the first building permit, if required by the Board of Supervisors as a condition of approval.
>
> \(3\) The applicant shall remain responsible for all applicable real estate taxes assessed on non-exempt improvements on the project site parcels as determined by the Lancaster County Board of Assessment Appeals.
>
> \(4\) The applicant shall remain responsible for all applicable school district real estate taxes, which shall not be subject to any PILOT agreement between the applicant and the Township. The Township shall have no authority to negotiate or enter into any agreement affecting school district tax revenues.
>
> \(5\) A property value impact assessment may be required at the discretion of the Board of Supervisors, to be prepared by a state-certified general appraiser retained by the Township at the applicant\'s expense. The assessment shall evaluate the potential impact of the proposed facility on the market value of residential properties within one thousand (1,000) feet of the project site boundary.

**Section 27-605(B)(14)(k). Scope of Approval**

> \(1\) A conditional use approval granted under this Section 27-605(B)(14) shall apply only to the project site as identified in the conditional use application and as depicted on the site plan approved by the Board of Supervisors. The conditional use approval shall not extend to, nor shall it authorize construction or operation of, any facilities, structures, or infrastructure located outside the boundaries of the project site.
>
> \(2\) Off-site infrastructure, including but not limited to generation tie lines, transmission lines, distribution lines, access roads located outside the project site boundary, and utility interconnection facilities not located on the parcels identified in the conditional use application, shall be subject to separate zoning, land development, subdivision, and permitting approvals as applicable under this Ordinance, the Conestoga Township Subdivision and Land Development Ordinance, the ordinances of adjacent municipalities through which such off-site infrastructure may be routed, and applicable state and federal law. The approval of a conditional use under this Section shall not constitute, nor shall it be construed as, approval of any off-site infrastructure.
>
> \(3\) Modification, expansion, or reconfiguration of the approved project beyond the scope of the approved site plan shall require either: (i) an amendment to the conditional use approval, to be reviewed and approved by the Board of Supervisors following the same substantive and procedural requirements as an original conditional use application under this Article VI, including public notice and hearing; or (ii) a new conditional use application filed and processed in accordance with this Article VI.
>
> \(4\) The conditional use approval shall be personal to the applicant identified in the conditional use application and the Decision and Order of the Board of Supervisors. The approval may be transferred or assigned to a successor, affiliate, or third party only with the prior written consent of the Board of Supervisors, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. The transferee or assignee shall assume all obligations, conditions, and requirements of the conditional use approval and shall demonstrate to the satisfaction of the Board of Supervisors that it has the financial, technical, and organizational capacity to construct, operate, and decommission the facility in accordance with the approved conditions.
>
> \(5\) The conditional use approval shall expire and shall be of no further force or effect if the applicant has not obtained a building permit for the utility-scale solar energy system within twenty-four (24) months of the date of the Decision and Order granting the conditional use approval, unless extended by the Board of Supervisors upon written request by the applicant filed prior to the expiration date and demonstrating good cause for the extension. Any extension granted by the Board of Supervisors shall not exceed an additional twelve (12) months.

**Section 27-605(B)(14)(l). Annual Reporting and Compliance Monitoring**

> \(1\) The applicant, or its successors or assigns approved by the Board of Supervisors, shall provide an annual report to the Board of Supervisors within sixty (60) days of each anniversary of the commercial operation date, summarizing: (i) facility operations, including total energy production in megawatt-hours (MWh) during the reporting period; (ii) maintenance activities performed during the reporting period, including any equipment replacements; (iii) compliance with all conditions of the conditional use approval and the provisions of this Ordinance; (iv) the current status and adequacy of the decommissioning security, including confirmation that the security remains in full force and effect; and (v) any material changes to the facility, its ownership, or its operations during the reporting period.
>
> \(2\) The Township Engineer, the Township Zoning Officer, or a designee of the Board of Supervisors shall be permitted to conduct an annual site inspection of the facility upon reasonable prior written notice to the applicant of not less than ten (10) business days. The applicant shall bear the reasonable cost of such inspection, including the fees of the Township Engineer. The annual inspection shall verify compliance with the conditions of the conditional use approval, including but not limited to screening and landscaping, fencing and security, noise and glare standards, stormwater management, and general site maintenance.
>
> \(3\) Failure to comply with any condition of the conditional use approval, any provision of this Section 27-605(B)(14), or any other applicable provision of this Ordinance may result in enforcement action by the Township, including but not limited to issuance of a notice of violation by the Township Zoning Officer, assessment of fines and penalties as authorized by this Ordinance and the Pennsylvania Municipalities Planning Code, or initiation of proceedings for revocation of the conditional use approval following a hearing before the Board of Supervisors. The Township shall provide the applicant with written notice of any alleged violation and a reasonable opportunity to cure, not to exceed thirty (30) days, prior to commencing revocation proceedings, except where the violation poses an imminent threat to public health, safety, or welfare.

**Section 27-605(B)(15)(c). Dimensional Standards for Energy Storage Facilities**

> \(3\) **Setback from Non-Participating Property Line.** An energy storage facility, including all battery enclosures, containers, inverters, transformers, thermal management systems, and associated support structures, shall be set back a minimum of three hundred (300) feet from any non-participating property line. **[Section 27-210. Definitions (Relevant Excerpt)]{.underline}**

The following definitions are excerpted from Section 27-210 (Definitions) of Chapter 27, to the extent they are relevant to the interpretation of Section 27-605(B)(14) and the conditions of any conditional use approval granted thereunder:

**\"Building Permit\"** --- A permit issued by the Township Zoning Officer, or by a designated third-party building code official, authorizing the construction, erection, alteration, modification, or demolition of any building or structure within the Township, in accordance with the applicable provisions of the Pennsylvania Uniform Construction Code, 34 Pa. Code Chapters 401-405, and this Ordinance. A building permit is distinct from and is not to be confused with a grading permit, a zoning permit, or any other permit issued by the Township.

**\"Grading Permit\"** --- A permit issued by the Township Zoning Officer authorizing earth-disturbing activities on a parcel, including but not limited to excavation, filling, grading, stockpiling of materials, and related activities. A grading permit may be issued separately from or concurrently with a building permit, depending on the scope and phasing of the proposed construction activity.

**\"Commencement of Construction\"** --- The initiation of physical construction activities on a project site, including but not limited to clearing, grubbing, grading, excavation, installation of foundations, driving of piles, or installation of any permanent structure or infrastructure component. The term \"commencement of construction\" shall not include surveying, geotechnical testing, soil sampling, environmental testing, installation of monitoring equipment, or other pre-construction investigative activities that do not involve significant physical disturbance of the land surface.

**\"Commercial Operation Date (COD)\"** --- With respect to a utility-scale solar energy system or energy storage facility, the date on which the facility first delivers electrical energy to the electrical grid for commercial sale pursuant to an executed power purchase agreement, interconnection agreement, or wholesale market participation agreement, as certified by the facility operator and confirmed by the applicable regional transmission organization or electric distribution company.

**CERTIFICATION**

CERTIFIED as a true and correct excerpt from the Conestoga Township Zoning Ordinance, Chapter 27 --- Zoning, Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, as amended through Ordinance No. 2023-12, adopted December 18, 2023, effective December 28, 2023. This excerpt includes Sections 27-601, 27-602, 27-605(A), 27-605(B)(14), 27-605(B)(15)(c)(3)-(4), and relevant definitions from Section 27-210.

CONESTOGA TOWNSHIP

By: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**

Name: Karen M. Brandt

Title: Township Secretary

Date: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**

This excerpt is provided for reference purposes only and does not constitute an official codification. In the event of any discrepancy between this excerpt and the official codified Conestoga Township Zoning Ordinance on file with the Township Secretary, the official codified ordinance shall control. Interested parties are encouraged to consult the complete Zoning Ordinance for all applicable provisions.

**PINNACLE RENEWABLES LLC** 4200 Commerce Parkway, Suite 310 Wilmington, DE 19801 Tel: (302) 555-8140 www.pinnaclerenewables.com

November 1, 2024

Honorable Harold Zimmerman, Chair and Members of the Board of Supervisors Conestoga Township 129 East Main Street Conestoga, PA 17516

**Re: Brightfield Solar Project --- Conditional Use Application, Response to Public Hearing Testimony and Summary of Proposed Conditions**

Dear Chairman Zimmerman and Members of the Board:

I write on behalf of Pinnacle Renewables LLC (\"Pinnacle\" or the \"Applicant\") and its wholly owned subsidiary, Brightfield Solar Project LLC (\"Brightfield Solar\" or the \"Project Company\"), a Pennsylvania limited liability company formed on March 15, 2024, in connection with the Conditional Use Application filed on June 3, 2024, for the Brightfield Solar Project (the \"Project\") under Section 27-605(B)(14) of the Conestoga Township Zoning Ordinance (the \"Ordinance\"), as amended in December 2023. The purpose of this letter is threefold: first, to provide a comprehensive summary of the Project for the Board\'s consideration; second, to respond substantively to the testimony and concerns raised by members of the public and neighboring property owners during the three public hearings held on August 14, September 11, and October 9, 2024; and third, to outline the Applicant\'s understanding of the proposed conditions of approval that the Board may wish to include in its decision, ahead of the Board\'s anticipated vote at its regularly scheduled meeting on November 18, 2024.

The Applicant acknowledges and appreciates the advisory recommendation issued by the Lancaster County Planning Commission on July 22, 2024, in which Director of Planning Thomas Reinhart rendered a generally favorable advisory opinion regarding the Project\'s consistency with the Lancaster County Comprehensive Plan and the Conestoga Township Zoning Ordinance. The Applicant has carefully reviewed the advisory recommendation and has incorporated several of Director Reinhart\'s suggestions into its revised project design and proposed conditions, as further described below. We believe the record developed over the course of these proceedings amply demonstrates that the Brightfield Solar Project satisfies all applicable standards for conditional use approval and will serve the public interest.

**[Project Summary]{.underline}**

The Brightfield Solar Project is a utility-scale solar energy generation facility utilizing single-axis tracking photovoltaic solar panel technology. The Project has a nameplate capacity of 120 megawatts alternating current (MW AC) and 156 megawatts direct current (MW DC), reflecting a DC-to-AC ratio of approximately 1.30. The facility will consist of approximately 296,000 solar modules mounted on single-axis tracker systems, served by 40 string inverters and 3 central power conversion stations. In addition to the solar generation components, the Application includes a 40 MW / 160 MWh battery energy storage system (\"BESS\") as a secondary use, which will enable the Project to provide dispatchable energy and grid reliability services.

The Project site encompasses approximately 850 acres across seven contiguous parcels situated in the Agricultural-Rural (A-R) zoning district. The fenced area of the facility will encompass approximately 720 acres, with solar panel coverage occupying approximately 580 acres of that area. The remaining acreage within the fence line will accommodate access roads, stormwater management facilities, the BESS compound, power conversion stations, and vegetative buffers.

The Project will interconnect to the regional transmission grid at the existing Conestoga Substation via a new 138 kV generation-tie line extending approximately 2.3 miles from the Project site. The Project holds queue position AG2-2024-0847 with Mid-Atlantic Grid Coordination LLC and is progressing through the interconnection study process.

The estimated total construction cost of the Project is approximately \$200 million, consisting of \$168 million for the solar generation facility and \$32 million for the BESS components. The Applicant\'s target date for commencement of construction is April 1, 2026, with a projected commercial operation date of December 31, 2027.

The seven parcels comprising the Project site are as follows:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Parcel ID**     **Owner(s)**                   **Acreage**       **Lease Term**
  ----------------- ------------------------------ ----------------- ----------------------------------
  120-45-001        Elmer J. & Ruth A. Stoltzfus   145 acres         35 years + two 5-year renewals

  120-45-002        Stoltzfus Family Trust         110 acres         35 years + two 5-year renewals

  120-45-003        Brubaker Agricultural LLC      130 acres         30 years + two 5-year renewals

  120-45-004        Brubaker Agricultural LLC      95 acres          30 years + two 5-year renewals

  120-45-005        David M. Herr                  120 acres         35 years + two 5-year renewals

  120-45-006        Lancaster Heritage Land Co.    140 acres         30 years + three 5-year renewals

  120-45-007        Lancaster Heritage Land Co.    110 acres         30 years + three 5-year renewals
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

All land lease agreements have been fully executed and are currently held in escrow with Commonwealth Title & Escrow LLC pending satisfaction of applicable conditions. The Revised Site Plan dated September 1, 2024, has been submitted as part of the application record and reflects the current project layout incorporating modifications made in response to Township staff and public comments received during the hearing process.

**[Response to Public Hearing Concerns]{.underline}**

Throughout the three public hearings, members of the public and neighboring property owners raised a number of substantive concerns regarding the Project. The Applicant takes these concerns seriously and has endeavored to address each category of concern through project design modifications, supplemental studies, and proposed conditions of approval. The following discussion addresses each principal area of concern in turn.

**A. Visual and Aesthetic Impact**

The Applicant acknowledges the concerns expressed by several neighboring property owners regarding the potential visual impact of the Project on the rural character of the surrounding landscape. In response, the Applicant has committed to installing a Type C vegetative screening buffer along the northern and eastern project boundaries, specifically in areas adjacent to non-participating properties containing occupied residences. The vegetative screening plan will incorporate a native species mix appropriate for the Lancaster County region, including species such as Eastern red cedar, American holly, and native viburnum varieties. All plantings will have a minimum installed height of four feet, with an expected mature height of twelve to fifteen feet, ensuring effective visual screening within three to five growing seasons. The Applicant is willing to work collaboratively with the Township and affected property owners in finalizing the screening plan to ensure that plantings are appropriately situated and maintained. In addition, the Project\'s perimeter fencing will be at least seven feet in height and will include wildlife passage openings at intervals no greater than 500 feet to facilitate the movement of small and medium-sized wildlife. The solar panels are designed with a maximum height of 14.5 feet at full tilt, which is well under any 20-foot height limitation applicable in the A-R district.

**B. Noise.** Several residents expressed concerns regarding potential noise impacts from the operation of the solar facility and BESS components. In response, the Applicant commissioned a comprehensive noise impact assessment prepared by Ridgepoint Environmental Consultants LLC, under the direction of Lead Consultant Priya Mukherjee. The noise study was conducted in accordance with ANSI/ASA S12.9-2013/Part 2 methodology, which established ambient sound level baselines at multiple receptor locations surrounding the Project site through continuous monitoring over a period of seven consecutive days. The study demonstrates that the facility, under worst-case operational scenarios --- including all 40 string inverters and all 3 central power conversion stations operating at full capacity simultaneously --- will not exceed 45 dBA at the nearest non-participating property line. The BESS components, including thermal management systems and associated auxiliary equipment, were also modeled as part of the worst-case scenario analysis. The results confirm that the combined operational noise from all Project components will remain within acceptable thresholds at all modeled receptor locations. Based on the findings of this study, the Applicant accepts a condition of approval limiting operational noise to 45 dBA at the nearest non-participating property line, as measured in accordance with the ANSI/ASA S12.9-2013/Part 2 standard referenced in the noise study.

**C. Property Values**

The Applicant acknowledges the concerns raised by neighboring property owners regarding potential impacts on residential property values. The Board will recall that a property value impact assessment was prepared by the Clarendon Appraisal Group, under the direction of Lead Appraiser Michael Engstrom, MAI, at the Township\'s direction and at the Applicant\'s expense. That study, which analyzed comparable sales data and utilized paired-sales methodology across multiple jurisdictions with existing utility-scale solar installations, concluded that there is no statistically significant negative impact on property values for residences located beyond 500 feet of a solar project boundary. The Applicant notes that the setback requirements proposed as conditions of approval provide additional protection: solar panels must be set back a minimum of 500 feet from any occupied dwelling on a non-participating parcel, and BESS components must be set back a minimum of 1,000 feet from any such dwelling. These generous setbacks substantially exceed the distances at which the Clarendon study found no measurable impact.

**D. Agricultural Land Preservation**

The Applicant acknowledges the deep significance of the Project\'s location on agricultural land and Pinnacle\'s sincere respect for the farming heritage of Lancaster County and Conestoga Township in particular. We recognize that the conversion of productive farmland to solar energy generation is a matter of legitimate concern for the community, and we have taken meaningful steps to mitigate the impact of the Project on the agricultural resource base.

Based on USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service soils mapping, 623 acres of the 850-acre Project site have been classified as prime agricultural land. In recognition of this, the Applicant has agreed to make an agricultural mitigation payment to the Lancaster Farmland Trust in the amount of \$1,200 per acre of prime agricultural land converted, for a total agricultural mitigation payment of \$747,600 (calculated as 623 acres multiplied by \$1,200 per acre). This payment will be made in full prior to commencement of construction and will support the Lancaster Farmland Trust\'s ongoing efforts to permanently preserve working farmland in Lancaster County through the acquisition of agricultural conservation easements.

In addition, the Project has been designed to maintain agricultural compatibility during its operational life. The Applicant intends to implement a managed grazing program utilizing sheep or, alternatively, to establish native pollinator habitat plantings under and between the panel rows, both of which have been demonstrated to provide meaningful ecological and agricultural co-benefits. Finally, the Applicant\'s decommissioning obligations, discussed further below, will ensure that the land can be fully restored to agricultural use at the end of the Project\'s useful life.

**E. Stormwater and Erosion**

The Applicant submitted a preliminary stormwater management plan as part of the Conditional Use Application. The plan was prepared in accordance with the Lancaster County Act 167 Stormwater Management Plan and the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection Chapter 102 requirements governing erosion and sediment control. A final stormwater management plan will be prepared and submitted for review and approval by the Lancaster County Conservation District, and subsequently to the Township Engineer, Gregory Shultz, P.E., of Fieldstone Engineering Associates, prior to issuance of any grading or building permits. The Applicant will obtain all required NPDES General Permit coverage (PAG-02) from the Pennsylvania DEP prior to commencement of earth disturbance activities. In addition, the Applicant will prepare and submit a comprehensive Erosion and Sedimentation Control Plan to the Lancaster County Conservation District for review and approval, and will ensure that all erosion and sediment control best management practices are installed and functioning prior to any land disturbance activities on the Project site.

**F. Traffic and Road Impacts**

The traffic impact study submitted with the Application demonstrates that the Project\'s construction phase will generate approximately 50 to 80 vehicle trips per day during peak construction activity, with vehicle types consisting primarily of construction worker personal vehicles, material delivery trucks, and specialized equipment transporters. During operations, traffic will decline substantially to approximately 2 to 5 vehicle trips per day for routine maintenance and monitoring activities. Construction access via Township roads will be coordinated with the Township Engineer, Gregory Shultz, P.E., to minimize disruption to local traffic patterns, and the Applicant will comply with all posted weight restrictions or, where necessary, seek appropriate permits for overweight loads.

To ensure that any road damage attributable to Project construction or operations is promptly repaired, the Applicant has agreed to post a road maintenance bond of \$500,000 during the construction period, to be reduced to \$100,000 during the operational period. The bond will remain in place for the duration of the Project\'s operational life and will be released only upon the Applicant\'s satisfactory completion of road restoration obligations as confirmed by the Township Engineer. Road improvement specifications will be developed in coordination with Gregory Shultz, P.E., and the Township\'s Road Department.

**[Environmental Compliance Summary]{.underline}**

The Applicant has completed or initiated the following environmental due diligence activities in connection with the Project:

**Phase I Environmental Site Assessment.** A Phase I Environmental Site Assessment was completed in May 2024 in accordance with ASTM E1527-21 standards. The assessment identified no Recognized Environmental Conditions (RECs), Controlled RECs, or Historical RECs on any of the seven parcels comprising the Project site.

**Cultural Resources Survey.** A cultural resources survey was completed in April 2024 by Ridgepoint Environmental Consultants LLC. The survey identified one potentially eligible historic resource --- the Stoltzfus Farmstead (circa 1847) --- located within approximately 200 feet of the Project boundary on parcel 120-45-001. The Applicant has initiated consultation with the Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission (\"PHMC\") regarding the Project\'s potential effects on this resource and is committed to completing a Section 106-equivalent review process in coordination with PHMC. The Applicant will obtain written confirmation from PHMC regarding the Project\'s effect on the Stoltzfus Farmstead, and any required mitigation measures, prior to commencement of any grading activities on parcels adjacent to the farmstead.

**Threatened and Endangered Species.** A Pennsylvania Natural Diversity Inventory (\"PNDI\") review identified potential habitat for the bog turtle (*Glyptemys muhlenbergii*), a federally listed threatened species, on parcels 120-45-003 and 120-45-004, both owned by Brubaker Agricultural LLC. Ridgepoint Environmental Consultants LLC is coordinating with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service regarding Phase 2 habitat assessment requirements for those parcels. The Applicant is committed to completing all necessary federal and state threatened and endangered species consultations and obtaining all required clearances prior to any land disturbance on those parcels.

**Solar Glare Analysis.** The Applicant will prepare and submit a solar glare analysis utilizing the Sandia National Laboratories GlareGauge tool (or equivalent), demonstrating that the Project will not produce significant glare impacts on public roadways or occupied residences within one mile of the Project boundary. The glare analysis will be submitted to the Township for review and comment prior to issuance of building permits.

**[Financial Assurances and Community Benefits]{.underline}**

**A. PILOT Agreement**

The Applicant has negotiated proposed Payment in Lieu of Taxes (\"PILOT\") terms with the Township. Under the proposed PILOT structure, the Applicant will pay \$385,000 per year for Years 1 through 15 of commercial operations. Commencing in Year 16, the annual PILOT payment will be subject to a 2% annual escalator, resulting in a Year 16 payment of \$392,700. The Applicant also remains responsible for all applicable Conestoga Valley School District real estate taxes assessed on non-exempt improvements associated with the Project. The estimated total annual tax revenue to the Township is approximately \$427,000, consisting of \$385,000 in PILOT payments and approximately \$42,000 in real estate taxes on non-exempt improvements. The formal PILOT agreement is being finalized in coordination with the Township Solicitor and will be executed in a form satisfactory to the Township prior to the issuance of any building permits for the Project.

**B. Decommissioning.** The Applicant is committed to the responsible decommissioning of the Project at the end of its useful life. The initial decommissioning cost estimate, prepared by a licensed professional engineer, projects a gross decommissioning cost of \$8.4 million, offset by an estimated salvage value of \$2.1 million for recyclable materials (principally steel, aluminum, copper, and silicon), yielding a net decommissioning cost of \$6.3 million. In accordance with the proposed conditions of approval, the Applicant will post decommissioning security in an amount equal to 125% of the net decommissioning cost, or \$7,875,000. This security will be posted prior to issuance of the first building permit for the Project. Acceptable forms of security include a surety bond, an irrevocable letter of credit, or an escrow account maintained at a financial institution rated A- or better by a nationally recognized credit rating agency. The Applicant is currently in discussions with Northbrook Surety Company regarding the issuance of a surety bond. The decommissioning cost estimate will be updated every five years by a licensed professional engineer, and the security amount will be adjusted accordingly. The decommissioning plan ensures that all above-ground and below-ground project components (to a depth of 36 inches) will be removed and the land restored to a condition suitable for agricultural use within 12 months of facility deactivation.

**C. Road Maintenance Bond**

As described in Section IV.F above, the Applicant has agreed to post a road maintenance bond of \$500,000 during the construction period, to be reduced to \$100,000 during the operational period, to address any road damage attributable to the Project.

**D. Agricultural Mitigation**

As described in Section IV.D above, the Applicant has agreed to make an agricultural mitigation payment of \$747,600 to the Lancaster Farmland Trust, calculated on the basis of 623 acres of prime agricultural land at \$1,200 per acre.

**[Summary of Applicant\'s Accepted Conditions]{.underline}**

The Applicant understands and accepts the following conditions of approval as discussed during the public hearing process and as recommended by the Lancaster County Planning Commission in its advisory letter dated July 22, 2024. The Applicant respectfully submits the following summary of its understanding of the principal conditions:

> 1\. **Setback Requirements.** Compliance with all applicable setback requirements, including: 100 feet from non-participating property lines for solar panels; 300 feet from non-participating property lines for BESS components; 150 feet from public road rights-of-way; 500 feet from occupied dwellings on non-participating parcels for solar panels; 1,000 feet from occupied dwellings on non-participating parcels for BESS components; and 250 feet from occupied dwellings on non-participating parcels for substations and inverter stations.
>
> 2\. **Vegetative Screening.** Installation and maintenance of a Type C vegetative screening buffer along the northern and eastern project boundaries adjacent to non-participating properties with occupied residences, utilizing native species with a minimum installed height of four feet.
>
> 3\. **Noise Limitation.** Operational noise shall not exceed 45 dBA at the nearest non-participating property line, as measured in accordance with the methodology set forth in the noise impact assessment.
>
> 4\. **Solar Glare Analysis.** Preparation and submission of a solar glare analysis demonstrating no significant glare impact on public roadways or occupied residences within one mile.
>
> 5\. **Decommissioning Security.** Posting of decommissioning security in the amount of \$7,875,000, representing 125% of the estimated net decommissioning cost of \$6.3 million, prior to issuance of the first building permit.
>
> 6\. **PILOT Agreement.** Execution of a PILOT agreement providing for annual payments of \$385,000 for Years 1 through 15, with a 2% annual escalator commencing in Year 16.
>
> 7\. **Road Maintenance Bond.** Posting of a road maintenance bond in the amount of \$500,000 during the construction period, reduced to \$100,000 during the operational period.
>
> 8\. **Agricultural Mitigation.** Payment of \$747,600 to the Lancaster Farmland Trust, representing an agricultural mitigation payment of \$1,200 per acre for 623 acres of prime agricultural land.
>
> 9\. **Stormwater Management.** Submission and approval of a final stormwater management plan by the Lancaster County Conservation District and the Township Engineer prior to issuance of grading permits.
>
> 10\. **Environmental and Cultural Resource Consultations.** Completion of all required consultations with the Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission and the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, and receipt of all necessary clearances, prior to commencement of land disturbance activities on affected parcels.
>
> 11\. **Perimeter Fencing.** Installation of perimeter fencing with a minimum height of seven feet, incorporating wildlife passage openings at intervals no greater than 500 feet.
>
> 12\. **NPDES and E&S Permits.** Obtaining all required NPDES and Erosion and Sedimentation Control permits from the Pennsylvania DEP and Lancaster County Conservation District.
>
> 13\. **Annual Reporting.** Submission of an annual report to the Board of Supervisors summarizing operational status, maintenance activities, complaint logs, and compliance with conditions of approval.
>
> 14\. **FAA Determination.** Obtaining an FAA determination of no hazard, if applicable, for any project structures exceeding 200 feet in height.
>
> 15\. **General Compliance.** Compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, regulations, and ordinances throughout the construction and operational life of the Project.

**[Closing and Request for Approval]{.underline}**

The Applicant wishes to express its sincere appreciation for the Board\'s thorough and diligent review of the Conditional Use Application, the meaningful engagement of members of the public throughout the hearing process, and the professionalism and responsiveness of Township staff in administering this proceeding. The Brightfield Solar Project represents a capital investment of approximately \$200 million in Conestoga Township, will generate an estimated \$427,000 in annual tax revenue to the Township and the Conestoga Valley School District, will support approximately 300 to 400 jobs during the peak construction period, and will provide long-term clean energy generation sufficient to power approximately 25,000 Pennsylvania homes.

The Applicant respectfully submits that the Brightfield Solar Project meets all applicable requirements of Section 27-605(B)(14) of the Conestoga Township Zoning Ordinance and the general conditional use standards set forth in Sections 603(c)(2) and 913.2 of the Pennsylvania Municipalities Planning Code, 53 P.S. §§ 10603(c)(2), 10913.2. On the basis of the record developed during this proceeding, the Applicant respectfully requests that the Board vote to approve the Conditional Use Application at its November 18, 2024 meeting, subject to the conditions summarized herein.

The Applicant\'s legal counsel, Christine Navarro, Esq., of Hathaway & Lowell LLP, and our environmental consultants at Ridgepoint Environmental Consultants LLC, remain available to address any additional questions the Board or Township staff may have in advance of the November 18 meeting.

Respectfully submitted,

By: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**

Derek Holcomb Vice President of Development Pinnacle Renewables LLC 4200 Commerce Parkway, Suite 310 Wilmington, DE 19801 Tel: (302) 555-8147

Email: dholcomb@pinnaclerenewables.com

cc: Christine Navarro, Esq., Hathaway & Lowell LLP cc: Priya Mukherjee, Ridgepoint Environmental Consultants LLC cc: Gregory Shultz, P.E., Fieldstone Engineering Associates cc: Margaret Tsai, CEO, Pinnacle Renewables LLC

**Enclosures:**

> 1\. Revised Site Plan (dated September 1, 2024)
>
> 2\. Noise Impact Assessment (Ridgepoint Environmental Consultants LLC; ANSI/ASA S12.9-2013/Part 2 methodology)

> 3\. Preliminary Stormwater Management Plan
>
> 4\. Decommissioning Cost Estimate and Plan

**LANCASTER COUNTY PLANNING COMMISSION** 150 North Queen Street, Suite 320 Lancaster, PA 17603

Telephone: (717) 299-8333 \| Facsimile: (717) 295-3659

July 22, 2024

Harold Zimmerman, Chair Conestoga Township Board of Supervisors Conestoga Township Municipal Building 1217 River Road Conestoga, PA 17516

**Re: Advisory Review and Recommendation --- Conditional Use Application No. CU-2024-012, Brightfield Solar Project, Pinnacle Renewables LLC**

Dear Chair Zimmerman:

The Lancaster County Planning Commission (\"Commission\") has completed its advisory review of Conditional Use Application No. CU-2024-012, filed by Pinnacle Renewables LLC (\"Applicant\") on June 3, 2024, for the proposed Brightfield Solar Project. This review was conducted pursuant to Section 609.1 of the Pennsylvania Municipalities Planning Code (Act 247, as amended), which requires that conditional use applications be referred to the county planning commission for advisory review and comment prior to final action by the governing body. This letter constitutes the Commission\'s non-binding advisory recommendation to the Conestoga Township Board of Supervisors. The application was reviewed at the Commission\'s regularly scheduled meeting on July 17, 2024, and the findings and recommendations set forth herein reflect the consensus of the Commission at that meeting. In preparing this letter, the Commission reviewed the application materials and supporting documentation submitted by the Applicant, the Conestoga Township Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 27, as amended December 2023), the applicable provisions of the Pennsylvania Municipalities Planning Code, and relevant county planning policies.

**[I. PROJECT SUMMARY]{.underline}**

The Applicant, Pinnacle Renewables LLC, is a Delaware limited liability company with principal offices at 4200 Commerce Parkway, Suite 310, Wilmington, DE 19801. The project entity is Brightfield Solar Project LLC, a Pennsylvania limited liability company and wholly owned subsidiary of Pinnacle Renewables LLC, which will serve as the owner and operator of the proposed facility. The proposed project consists of a 120 MW AC (156 MW DC) single-axis tracking photovoltaic solar energy facility with an optional 40 MW / 160 MWh battery energy storage system (\"BESS\"). The facility would be located on approximately 850 acres across seven contiguous parcels situated in the Agricultural-Rural (A-R) zoning district of Conestoga Township, Lancaster County, Pennsylvania. The parcels comprising the project site are identified as follows:

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Parcel ID**           **Owner(s)**                   **Acreage**
  ----------------------- ------------------------------ -----------------------
  120-45-001              Elmer J. & Ruth A. Stoltzfus   185.3 acres

  120-45-002              Stoltzfus Family Trust         142.7 acres

  120-45-003              Brubaker Agricultural LLC      210.4 acres

  120-45-004              Brubaker Agricultural LLC      98.6 acres

  120-45-005              David M. Herr                  75.2 acres

  120-45-006              Lancaster Heritage Land Co.    88.9 acres

  120-45-007              Lancaster Heritage Land Co.    48.9 acres
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The project as proposed includes approximately 296,000 solar modules mounted on single-axis tracking structures, 40 string inverters, and 3 central power conversion stations. The total fenced area encompasses approximately 720 acres, with panel coverage of approximately 580 acres. Perimeter fencing will consist of 7-foot chain-link fencing with wildlife passage openings at approximately 500-foot intervals. Electrical interconnection to the regional transmission grid will be accomplished via a 2.3-mile, 138 kV generation tie line (\"gen-tie line\") connecting the project substation to the existing Conestoga Substation. The Applicant holds interconnection queue position AG2-2024-0847 with Mid-Atlantic Grid Coordination LLC.

The estimated total project cost is approximately \$200 million, consisting of approximately \$168 million for the solar facility and approximately \$32 million for the BESS. The projected commercial operation date is December 31, 2027. Pursuant to Section 27-605(B)(14) of the Conestoga Township Zoning Ordinance, solar energy systems exceeding 10 MW in generating capacity are classified as a Conditional Use in the Agricultural-Rural (A-R) zoning district, thereby requiring approval by the Board of Supervisors following public hearings.

**[II. CONSISTENCY WITH COUNTY COMPREHENSIVE PLAN]{.underline}**

The Commission has evaluated the proposed Brightfield Solar Project for general consistency with the policies and objectives of the Lancaster County Comprehensive Plan. The County Comprehensive Plan supports the diversification of energy sources throughout the county and encourages the responsible siting of renewable energy facilities in a manner that balances economic development with the preservation of community character and natural resources. The Commission acknowledges the inherent tension between renewable energy development and the preservation of agricultural land, which remains a core priority of the County Comprehensive Plan. The project site consists primarily of prime agricultural soils, with approximately 623 acres classified as prime agricultural land under the United States Department of Agriculture Natural Resources Conservation Service soil classifications.

While the proposed project will convert a significant area of prime agricultural land to solar energy use for the duration of the project\'s operational life, the Commission notes that the land lease agreements submitted by the Applicant provide for decommissioning and full restoration of the land to agricultural condition following the useful life of the facility. The reversible nature of the land use conversion is an important consideration in the Commission\'s assessment. Nevertheless, the Commission recommends that the Township require an agricultural mitigation payment to offset the temporary conversion of prime agricultural land, with such payment directed to Lancaster Farmland Trust at a rate consistent with prevailing agricultural conservation easement values in Lancaster County. The Commission finds that, on balance, the proposed project is generally consistent with the County Comprehensive Plan, subject to conditions sufficient to mitigate impacts on agricultural resources, neighboring properties, and community infrastructure.

**[III. REVIEW FINDINGS AND RECOMMENDATIONS]{.underline}**

The Commission offers the following specific findings and recommendations for the Township\'s consideration in its deliberations on this application.

**A. Setbacks and Dimensional Requirements**

The Commission has reviewed the Applicant\'s site plan in relation to the setback and dimensional requirements established by Section 27-605(B)(14) of the Conestoga Township Zoning Ordinance. Based on the materials submitted, the Commission finds that the site plan generally complies with the applicable setback requirements as follows: solar panels are set back a minimum of 100 feet from any non-participating property line; solar infrastructure is set back a minimum of 150 feet from any public road right-of-way; all solar components are located a minimum of 500 feet from any occupied dwelling on a non-participating parcel; and substation and inverter equipment are set back a minimum of 250 feet from any non-participating property line. With respect to the battery energy storage system, the proposed battery energy storage system setback of 250 feet from non-participating property lines is consistent with the ordinance. The BESS is also set back a minimum of 1,000 feet from any occupied dwelling on a non-participating parcel, which satisfies the ordinance requirement for energy storage facilities in proximity to residential structures. The proposed solar panel maximum height at full tilt is 14.5 feet, which is well within the 20-foot maximum height permitted by the ordinance. The Commission recommends that the Township confirm that all setbacks are accurately depicted on the final site plan prior to the issuance of any building or zoning permits.

**B. Screening and Visual Mitigation**

The Commission recommends the installation of vegetative screening buffers along all project boundaries adjacent to non-participating properties with occupied residences, with particular attention to the northern and eastern boundaries of the project site where the proximity to existing residential structures is greatest. The Commission recommends a Type C vegetative screening buffer utilizing native species, with a minimum planting height of 4 feet at the time of installation and an expected mature height of 12 to 15 feet. The screening plan should be reviewed and approved by the Township Engineer prior to implementation. The Commission considers visual screening to be an important measure for community acceptance and the protection of neighboring property values. The Commission notes that the Township has retained Clarendon Appraisal Group (Michael Engstrom, MAI) to prepare a property value impact assessment and encourages completion of that assessment prior to final action on the conditional use application. Visual screening buffers should be installed along all required frontages to ensure adequate mitigation of visual impacts on surrounding properties and public roadways.

**C. Stormwater Management**

Given the scale of the proposed project, the Commission recommends that the Applicant submit a comprehensive stormwater management plan prepared in accordance with the Pennsylvania Stormwater Best Management Practices Manual and the Lancaster County Act 167 Stormwater Management Plan. The stormwater management plan should be reviewed and approved by both the Lancaster County Conservation District and the Township Engineer, Gregory Shultz, P.E., of Fieldstone Engineering Associates. The Commission notes particular concern regarding the extent of impervious and semi-impervious surface coverage, as approximately 580 acres of panel coverage has the potential to concentrate and redirect stormwater runoff in ways that may adversely affect adjacent agricultural operations and downstream waterways. The Commission recommends post-construction stormwater monitoring for a minimum period of three years following the commencement of commercial operations. The Applicant should obtain an NPDES General Permit (PAG-02) prior to any land disturbance activities, and the Township should require an Erosion and Sedimentation Control Plan approved by the Lancaster County Conservation District as a condition of any grading or building permit.

**D. Environmental and Cultural Resources**

The Applicant submitted a Phase I Environmental Site Assessment completed in May 2024, which indicated no Recognized Environmental Conditions (RECs) on the project site. A Cultural Resources Survey was completed by Ridgepoint Environmental Consultants LLC (Priya Mukherjee, Lead Consultant) in April 2024. That survey identified one potentially eligible historic resource --- the Stoltzfus Farmstead, dating to approximately 1847 --- located within 200 feet of the project boundary. The Commission recommends that the Township require formal consultation with the Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission (PHMC) regarding the Stoltzfus Farmstead and obtain written confirmation of no adverse effect prior to the issuance of any grading permits for adjacent areas.

Additionally, the Pennsylvania Natural Diversity Inventory (PNDI) review conducted by the Applicant identified potential habitat for the bog turtle (*Glyptemys muhlenbergii*), a species listed as threatened under the federal Endangered Species Act, on parcels 120-45-003 and 120-45-004. The Commission recommends that the Township require completion of all necessary federal and state consultations regarding threatened and endangered species prior to any land disturbance on the affected parcels. The Applicant should coordinate directly with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service regarding potential bog turtle habitat and provide documentation of the outcome of such consultation to the Township.

**E. Decommissioning.** The Commission recommends that the Township require a comprehensive decommissioning plan and adequate financial security to ensure removal of the facility and restoration of the site at the end of the project\'s useful life. The Applicant has submitted a preliminary decommissioning cost estimate of \$8.4 million (gross) less \$2.1 million in anticipated salvage value, yielding a net decommissioning cost estimate of \$6.3 million. The Commission recommends that the Township require financial security in an amount equal to at least 125% of the estimated net decommissioning cost, which would equal \$7,875,000 at current estimates. The decommissioning cost estimate should be updated every five years by a licensed professional engineer, with corresponding adjustments to the required financial security. Acceptable forms of financial security should include a surety bond, an irrevocable letter of credit, or a funded escrow account held at a creditworthy financial institution. Financial security should be posted prior to the issuance of the first building permit for the project.

**F. Infrastructure and Road Impacts**

Construction of a project of this scale and cost --- estimated at \$200 million --- will generate significant heavy vehicle traffic during the construction period, with the potential to cause damage to local Township roads. The Commission recommends that the Applicant be required to post a road maintenance bond for the duration of the construction period to protect Township roads from damage. The Applicant should conduct pre-construction and post-construction road condition surveys on all designated construction traffic routes, and the Township and Applicant should execute a formal road maintenance agreement addressing road repair obligations, load limits, traffic routing, and scheduling of construction activities. Coordination with the Township Engineer on these matters is essential. The Commission also notes that the proposed 2.3-mile, 138 kV gen-tie line to the Conestoga Substation traverses land outside the project site and may require additional approvals or coordination with affected landowners and potentially adjacent municipalities. The Township should confirm that all necessary easements and approvals for the gen-tie line are secured by the Applicant.

**[IV. NOISE AND GLARE]{.underline}**

The Commission recommends that the Township impose a noise limit of 45 dBA measured at the nearest non-participating property line, consistent with the performance standards established in the Conestoga Township Zoning Ordinance. The Commission notes that the Applicant has submitted a noise study as part of the application materials. The Commission further recommends that a solar glare analysis be completed to assess potential glare impacts on public roadways and occupied residences within the vicinity of the project site. The Applicant should demonstrate that no significant glare impact will result within one mile of the project boundary, and the Township should consider requiring mitigation measures if the analysis identifies areas of concern.

**[V. FINANCIAL AND COMMUNITY BENEFIT CONSIDERATIONS]{.underline}**

The Commission notes the Applicant\'s proposed payment in lieu of taxes (\"PILOT\") agreement with the Township, which provides for annual payments of \$385,000 for Years 1 through 15, with a 2% annual escalator thereafter for the remaining term of the project. The total estimated annual revenue to the Township, inclusive of the PILOT and real estate taxes on non-exempt improvements, is approximately \$427,000. The Commission encourages the Township to negotiate a PILOT agreement that reflects the scale, duration, and community impact of the project, and to consider directing a portion of the PILOT revenue to community benefit purposes. Additionally, and as noted above, the Commission recommends an agricultural mitigation payment to Lancaster Farmland Trust to offset the conversion of approximately 623 acres of prime agricultural land. The Commission further notes the potential for local economic benefits during the construction period associated with the estimated \$200 million project investment. The Applicant should be encouraged to provide annual reports to the Township regarding project operations, revenue payments, and compliance with conditions of approval.

**[VI. OVERALL RECOMMENDATION]{.underline}**

Based on the foregoing review, the Lancaster County Planning Commission recommends **approval** of Conditional Use Application No. CU-2024-012 for the Brightfield Solar Project, **subject to conditions** addressing the matters identified in this letter, including but not limited to agricultural mitigation, vegetative screening, stormwater management, environmental and cultural resource protection, decommissioning financial security, road maintenance, noise limits, and glare mitigation. This recommendation is advisory and non-binding pursuant to Section 609.1 of the Pennsylvania Municipalities Planning Code. The final determination on the conditional use application rests solely with the Conestoga Township Board of Supervisors following the completion of public hearings as required by law. The Commission encourages the Township to give careful consideration to the recommendations set forth herein in formulating any conditions of approval. The Commission remains available to provide additional technical assistance upon request.

Respectfully submitted,

LANCASTER COUNTY PLANNING COMMISSION

By: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**

Thomas Reinhart Director of Planning

Date: July 22, 2024

**cc:**

> Barbara Kreider, Zoning Hearing Officer, Lancaster County Planning Commission Derek Holcomb, Vice President of Development, Pinnacle Renewables LLC Gregory Shultz, P.E., Fieldstone Engineering Associates (Township Engineer) Conestoga Township Board of Supervisors (all members)
