=====TOWNSHIP SOLICITOR=====
From: Allen Driscoll, Esq. <adriscoll@driscoll-frey.com>
To: Christine Navarro <cnavarro@hathaway-lowell.com>
Cc: Harold Zimmerman <hzimmerman@conestogatwp.org>; Derek Holcomb <dholcomb@pinnaclerenewables.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jan 2025 03:47:00 -0000
Subject: Brightfield Solar Project — PILOT Agreement: Outstanding Issues
Content-Type: text/plain; charset="utf-8"
Content-Transfer-Encoding: quoted-printable
MIME-Version: 1.0

Christine,

I hope the new year is treating you well. I wanted to follow up on the PILOT =
agreement negotiations for the Brightfield Solar Project now that we have cle=
ared a significant procedural milestone.

As you know, the Board of Supervisors issued its Decision and Order on Decemb=
er 6, 2024, granting conditional use approval to Pinnacle Renewables LLC and =
Brightfield Solar Project LLC for the project. The 30-day appeal period under=
 Section 914.1 of the Pennsylvania Municipalities Planning Code expired on Ja=
nuary 5, 2025, and no appeal was filed. The Decision is now final. With that =
behind us, I want to turn our attention to resolving the remaining open issue=
s on the PILOT agreement so we can get it across the finish line. As you are =
aware, Condition 30 of the Decision requires execution of a PILOT agreement "=
in a form satisfactory to the Township Solicitor" prior to issuance of any bu=
ilding permits for the project. I have received and reviewed the most recent =
draft PILOT agreement your office circulated on January 8, 2025, and I have g=
one through it in detail with Chairman Zimmerman and the full Board of Superv=
isors.

**Agreed Terms =E2=80=94 General Framework**

Let me start with the good news. The parties appear to have reached agreement=
 on the core PILOT structure, and I want to memorialize that common ground. W=
e are aligned on the following: an annual payment of $385,000 per year during=
 the initial period, payable in lieu of real property taxes on the solar faci=
lity and battery energy storage system (BESS) components. This PILOT is separ=
ate from and in addition to real estate taxes on non-exempt improvements, whi=
ch we estimate at approximately $42,000 per year and which Brightfield Solar =
Project LLC will continue to pay through the normal assessment process. Schoo=
l district real estate taxes are not subject to the PILOT and remain payable =
in full. Taken together, the total estimated annual revenue to the Township f=
rom the project is approximately $427,000 ($385,000 PILOT + $42,000 real esta=
te taxes). We also agree that the agreement should identify Brightfield Solar=
 Project LLC =E2=80=94 the Pennsylvania LLC and project SPE =E2=80=94 as the =
obligor, and that the PILOT term should be coterminous with the useful life o=
f the facility or the duration of the conditional use approval, whichever is =
shorter. All of this is consistent with how your January 8 draft is structure=
d, and we have no quarrel with those provisions.

That said, there are two substantive issues that remain open, and I need to f=
lag both as material from the Township's perspective.

**Open Issue #1 =E2=80=94 Most-Favored-Nation Clause**

The Township continues to request inclusion of a most-favored-nation ("MFN") =
clause in the PILOT agreement. As we discussed during our call in December, t=
he Board's position is straightforward: if any other utility-scale solar ener=
gy project in Lancaster County enters into a PILOT or similar tax agreement w=
ith any municipality in the county at a per-MW or per-acre rate that exceeds =
the Brightfield rate, the Brightfield PILOT payment would be automatically ad=
justed upward to match the higher rate. Chairman Zimmerman and the Board are =
particularly focused on this point because the Brightfield project is one of =
the first large-scale solar facilities in Lancaster County. The Township does=
 not want to find itself locked into below-market terms if the market for sol=
ar PILOTs evolves over the next several years =E2=80=94 and given the pace of=
 development in the region, it very likely will. For reference, the project's=
 current PILOT rate works out to approximately $3,208 per MW per year ($385,0=
00 =C3=B7 120 MW), or approximately $453 per acre per year ($385,000 =C3=B7 8=
50 acres). The Township wants assurance that these figures remain competitive=
 over the life of the agreement. I understand that your January 8 draft rejec=
ted the MFN clause, and I have reviewed Pinnacle's position that such a claus=
e creates uncertainty for project financing and investor returns. We take tha=
t concern seriously, but the Township considers this a material term. I would=
 ask that you and Derek reconsider the MFN provision, or alternatively propos=
e a protective mechanism that addresses the Township's concern =E2=80=94 for =
example, a periodic rate review at defined intervals, or a floor-and-cap stru=
cture that provides some upside protection while giving Pinnacle a ceiling fo=
r budgeting purposes. I should also note that the Township is aware Pinnacle =
Renewables has a 2.4 GW development pipeline across Mid-Atlantic Grid Coordin=
ation LLC territory and may be developing other projects in Lancaster County.=
 The MFN clause would simply ensure consistent treatment across those project=
s and give the Board confidence that Conestoga Township is not disadvantaged =
by being an early mover.

**Open Issue #2 =E2=80=94 Escalator Commencement Date**

The second open issue is the commencement date for the 2% annual escalation o=
f the PILOT payment. The Township's position is that the 2% annual escalator =
should begin in Year 11 of the PILOT term =E2=80=94 meaning the PILOT payment=
 would remain at $385,000 per year for Years 1 through 10, and then increase =
by 2% per year starting in Year 11. Your January 8 draft, by contrast, provid=
es that the 2% annual escalator does not begin until Year 16, holding the pay=
ment flat at $385,000 for the first 15 years with escalation commencing only =
in Year 16. The financial significance of this disagreement is not trivial. U=
nder the Township's proposed Year 11 start, the Year 11 payment would be $392=
,700, and by Year 15 the payment would reach approximately $425,048 ($385,000=
 =C3=97 1.02^5). Under Pinnacle's proposed Year 16 start, payments remain fla=
t at $385,000 through Year 15, with the first escalated payment of $392,700 n=
ot arriving until Year 16. The cumulative difference over the first 15 years =
is significant to the Township's long-term revenue projections and budget pla=
nning. The Township's view is that a Year 11 escalator is eminently reasonabl=
e given the anticipated operational life of 30-plus years and the inevitable =
erosion of purchasing power from inflation over that period. I will note that=
 the Decision and Order references "negotiated PILOT terms" but does not spec=
ify the escalator commencement year, so this is a point for the agreement its=
elf to resolve. However, I want to be direct: Condition 30 requires the PILOT=
 agreement to be "in a form satisfactory to the Township Solicitor," and I am=
 not in a position to certify satisfaction until both of these issues =E2=80=
=94 the MFN clause and the escalator start date =E2=80=94 are resolved in a m=
anner acceptable to the Board.

**Timeline and Next Steps**

I want to be mindful of the project timeline. My understanding is that Pinnac=
le is targeting an April 1, 2026 construction start date, and given that buil=
ding permits cannot be issued without an executed PILOT agreement under Condi=
tion 30, we should aim to finalize the agreement well in advance to avoid any=
 permitting delays. I would suggest that we schedule a call or, if preferable=
, an in-person meeting within the next two weeks to discuss these two outstan=
ding issues and see if we can find a path forward. I am available the week of=
 January 27, 2025 =E2=80=94 please let me know what works on your end. Chairm=
an Zimmerman has indicated his willingness to participate in a meeting if it =
would be helpful to resolve these issues at the supervisors' level, and I exp=
ect Derek may want to be involved as well.

Upon resolution of these two open items, I believe the balance of the agreeme=
nt is in good shape and we should be able to finalize and circulate for execu=
tion within 30 days.

I want to close by reiterating that the Township remains fully supportive of =
the Brightfield Solar Project and recognizes the significant economic benefit=
s it will bring to Conestoga Township =E2=80=94 including the annual PILOT an=
d tax revenues, construction-phase employment, and the agricultural mitigatio=
n payment to the Lancaster Farmland Trust. These are meaningful contributions=
, and the Board appreciates Pinnacle's commitment to the community. I am hope=
ful we can resolve these remaining issues collaboratively and get the agreeme=
nt signed.

Please let me know your thoughts and your availability for a meeting. I look =
forward to hearing from you.

Best regards,

Allen Driscoll, Esq.
Driscoll & Frey LLP
45 East King Street, Suite 200
Lancaster, PA 17602
Phone: (717) 555-0184
Email: adriscoll@driscoll-frey.com

*Counsel to Conestoga Township*

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""Builds compliance-tracking-matrix.docx for Brightfield Solar Project CU-2024-006."""
import docx

SLATE = RGBColor(0x44, 0x54, 0x6A)
GREY = RGBColor(0x59, 0x59, 0x59)
WHITE = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
def shade(cell, hexfill):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = OxmlElement('w:shd')
    shd.set(qn('w:val'), 'clear'); shd.set(qn('w:color'), 'auto'); shd.set(qn('w:fill'), hexfill)
    tcPr.append(shd)

def cell_margins(table, top=40, bottom=40, left=70, right=70):
    tblPr = table._tbl.tblPr
    mar = OxmlElement('w:tblCellMar')
    for tag, val in (('top', top), ('left', left), ('bottom', bottom), ('right', right)):
        el = OxmlElement('w:' + tag); el.set(qn('w:w'), str(val)); el.set(qn('w:type'), 'dxa'); mar.append(el)
    tblPr.append(mar)

def repeat_header(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    el = OxmlElement('w:tblHeader'); el.set(qn('w:val'), 'true'); trPr.append(el)

def no_split(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    el = OxmlElement('w:cantSplit'); el.set(qn('w:val'), 'true'); trPr.append(el)

def fixed_layout(table):
    tblPr = table._tbl.tblPr
    layout = OxmlElement('w:tblLayout'); layout.set(qn('w:type'), 'fixed'); tblPr.append(layout)

def set_widths(table, widths):
    fixed_layout(table)
    table.autofit = False
    for row in table.rows:
        for i, w in enumerate(widths):
            if i < len(row.cells):
                row.cells[i].width = Inches(w)

def write(cell, text, size=7.4, bold=False, color=None, align=None, italic=False, space_after=0):

    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
    p.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.0
    if align is not None:
        p.alignment = align
    parts = text.split("\n")
    for i, part in enumerate(parts):
        if i > 0:
            p = cell.add_paragraph()
            p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(0); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
            p.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.0
            if align is not None:
                p.alignment = align
        run = p.add_run(part)
        run.font.size = Pt(size); run.bold = bold; run.italic = italic
        run.font.name = 'Calibri'
        if color is not None:
            run.font.color.rgb = color

def table(doc, headers, rows, widths, status_col=None, status_map=None, size=7.4,
          header_size=7.4, bold_first=True, zebra=True, first_col_bold=False):

    return p

    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(0); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)

    return p

def caption(doc, text):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(2); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    r = p.add_run(text); r.font.size = Pt(7.8); r.italic = True; r.font.color.rgb = GREY; r.font.name = 'Calibri'
    return p

def add_field(paragraph, instr):
    run = paragraph.add_run()
    f1 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); f1.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'begin')
    it = OxmlElement('w:instrText'); it.set(qn('xml:space'), 'preserve'); it.text = instr
    f2 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); f2.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'end')
    run._r.append(f1); run._r.append(it); run._r.append(f2)
    run.font.size = Pt(7.5); run.font.name = 'Calibri'; run.font.color.rgb = GREY

def new_section(doc, landscape=False):
    sec = doc.add_section(WD_SECTION.NEW_PAGE)
    if landscape:
        sec.orientation = WD_ORIENT.LANDSCAPE
        sec.page_width, sec.page_height = Inches(11), Inches(8.5)
        sec.left_margin = sec.right_margin = Inches(0.35)
        sec.top_margin = Inches(0.5); sec.bottom_margin = Inches(0.45)
    else:
        sec.orientation = WD_ORIENT.PORTRAIT
        sec.page_width, sec.page_height = Inches(8.5), Inches(11)
        sec.left_margin = sec.right_margin = Inches(0.85)
        sec.top_margin = Inches(0.7); sec.bottom_margin = Inches(0.65)
    return sec

def header_footer(doc, title):
    for sec in doc.sections:
        sec.header.is_linked_to_previous = False
        sec.footer.is_linked_to_previous = False
        hp = sec.header.paragraphs[0]
        hp.text = ""
        hp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT
        r = hp.add_run(title); r.font.size = Pt(7.2); r.font.color.rgb = GREY; r.font.name = 'Calibri'
        fp = sec.footer.paragraphs[0]
        fp.text = ""
        fp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
        r = fp.add_run("Brightfield Solar Project \u2014 Conditional Use Compliance Tracking Matrix  |  Application No. CU-2024-006  |  Rev. 1 \u2014 status as of 15 January 2025  |  Page ")
        r.font.size = Pt(7.2); r.font.color.rgb = GREY; r.font.name = 'Calibri'

        r = fp.add_run(" of "); r.font.size = Pt(7.2); r.font.color.rgb = GREY; r.font.name = 'Calibri'
        add_field(fp, 'NUMPAGES')
        r = fp.add_run("  |  Not legal advice \u2014 see \u00a72.6 Limitations"); r.font.size = Pt(7.2); r.font.color.rgb = GREY; r.font.name = 'Calibri'

  screening to the northern and eastern boundaries adjacent to residences. It omits the roadway-

  the security and the mitigation payment to the first building permit; Condition 34 keys them to 60 days
  before construction. The Ordinance separately defines a grading permit, and “commencement of
  construction” includes clearing and grading, so site disturbance could begin before the $7.9 million

assurance architecture and its mitigation scheme, and it adds reporting, testing and emergency-planning

be revisited as a whole. What the review does show is that the operative text of the conditions, rather than
the findings that support them, has drifted from the Ordinance in six identifiable places, and that the
record supporting the Decision has not been assembled in a form that would withstand an enforcement
challenge.

{"command": "cd $WORKSPACE_DIR/work && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='build.py'; s=open(p).read()

# Part C intro addition
anchor = '''h2(doc, "C.1  Register summary by type")'''
add = '''body(doc, "Read across the six sources, the pattern is consistent. The Ordinance-facing defects (Part B) are the structural ones. The Applicant's cover letter is the most "
          "divergent single source: application acreage, lease extension terms, noise-study authorship, the operational bond amount, revenue attribution and the mitigation "
          "recital all differ from the Decision. The Planning Commission letter contributes the application-number conflict and the 250 ft BESS statement. The two 2025 "
          "implementation emails contribute the escalator dispute, two citation variants and two factual slips. A final group is internal to the Decision itself: the "
          "620/623 recital, the $150,000/$100,000 bond, the assurance-timing conflict, and a BESS that is described as optional but approved as required.", size=8.8)
'''
assert anchor in s
s = s.replace(anchor, add + anchor, 1)

# Dissent cross-check before 1.3
anchor2 = '''h2(doc, "1.3  Priority actions")'''
add2 = '''h2(doc, "1.3  Cross-check against the dissenting opinion")
body(doc, "Supervisors Beiler and Lapp dissented on three grounds: the incompatibility of an 850-acre facility converting about 623 acres of prime farmland with the A-R "
          "district; the adequacy of the property-value evidence; and the sufficiency of the conditions, with specific reference to screening and to the long-term effects "
          "of the battery storage system. Those three objections map onto risks this review reached independently \\u2014 R-08 (mitigation base), R-06 (screening narrower than "
          "the Ordinance), R-10 (coverage) and R-14 (BESS status and approvals). The dissent is therefore not merely a difference of aesthetic judgment: on screening and on "
          "the BESS, the operative conditions do not deliver what the majority's findings assume.", size=9.0, space_after=6)
h2(doc, "1.4  Priority actions")'''
s = s.replace(anchor2, add2, 1)
open(p,'w').write(s); print("ok")
EOF

{"file_path": "response.md", "content": "# Brightfield Solar Project — Compliance Tracking Matrix and Cross-Reference Analysis

**Deliverable:** `compliance-tracking-matrix.docx` (39 pages, Word; validated against ECMA‑376 WordprocessingML)

## What the document is

A working compliance register for Conditional Use Application No. CU‑2024‑006 (Decision and Order dated 6 December 2024), built from all six documents in the file: the Decision, the Zoning Ordinance excerpt (§ 27‑605(B)(14) et seq.), the Lancaster County Planning Commission advisory letter, the Applicant's 1 November 2024 cover letter, and the Township Engineer (10 Jan 2025) and Township Solicitor (15 Jan 2025) emails. Status is stated **as at 15 January 2025**, the date of the most recent source.

## Structure

| Part | Contents |
|---|---|
| 1–2 | Executive summary (snapshot counts, ten headline findings, cross-check against the dissent, priority actions); scope, source inventory, method, status/risk definitions, limitations |
| **Part A** | **Condition compliance tracking matrix** — all 35 conditions, each mapped to its Ordinance provision, responsible party, trigger/deadline, the evidence that would close it, status, risk and cross-references |
| **Part B** | **Ordinance conformance register** — 89 provisions of §§ 27‑602, 27‑605(B)(14) and 27‑605(B)(15) tested against the Decision (31 meets/exceeds, 25 partial, 6 unverified, 9 conflict, 16 not addressed, 2 n/a) |
| **Part C** | **Cross-reference register of inconsistencies** — 55 logged discrepancies with the quoted document values, the quantified variance, the controlling source and the disposition (51 still open) |
| **Part D** | **Independent recomputation schedule** — 39 figures, rates and date intervals recalculated from first principles with the formula shown |
| **Part E** | **Risk register** — 22 risks with likelihood/impact ratings (6 critical, 8 high, 7 medium, 1 low), owners and responses |
| **Part F** | Compliance deadline calendar with derivations and consequences of default |
| **Part G** | 22 open information requests |
| **Part H** | 16 prioritised recommendations with owners and timing |
| **Part I** | Assumptions, legal characterisations (for the Solicitor) and open questions — kept separate from extraction and arithmetic |
| Appendices | Source-to-deliverable traceability, defined terms, revision history and sign-off |

## Most significant findings

1. **Equipment setbacks fall below the Ordinance.** Condition 6 exempts string inverters from the 250 ft property-line setback (100 ft instead — a 60% reduction) and no condition imposes the Ordinance's **500 ft occupied-dwelling setback for substations, inverters and conversion stations** (a 50% shortfall if built to the condition). The Applicant's cover letter repeats the 250 ft figure *as a dwelling setback*, suggesting the error travelled from application into conditions.
2. **The mitigation the Board relied on is narrower than the Ordinance.** Condition 16 covers only north/east boundaries beside residences and omits the roadway-frontage buffers, the 30 ft width, the 60% evergreen floor and the 75%/5-year opacity standard — yet Findings 19 and Conclusions 4 and 6 rest on that screening.
3. **Financial assurances have two start dates.** Conditions 22 and 28 key security and mitigation to the *building* permit; Condition 34 keys them to 60 days before construction. Because the Ordinance defines *grading* permits separately, 850 acres could be cleared before the $7.9M security, the $747,600 payment or the PILOT are in place.
4. **Condition 10 is unperformable as sequenced** — submission by 6 March 2025 after Conservation District approval, where CD review takes 60–90 days (Engineer's estimate); the package would have had to be filed on or about the date of the Decision.
5. **The PILOT blocks every permit and is unresolved**: the Order says the 2% escalator starts after Year 15; the Township wants Year 11 (≈ $118,600 over Years 11–15); the Ordinance's statutory predicate (an exemption/abatement election) is undocumented and recording is not required.
6. **Decommissioning protections are weaker and shorter-fused**: 18-month restoration against the Ordinance's 12; 12 + 18 = 30 months breaches the 24-month absolute cap; 90-day security updates against 60; the 75%-of-gross floor, A.M. Best A‑VII surety rating and Township escrow beneficiary are missing.
7. **Arithmetic and record defects that should be corrected now**: Condition 28 recites 620 acres but pays on 623 ($3,600); the cover letter states a $100,000 operational road bond against the Order's $150,000; the Solicitor's Year 15 figure is $23 low; the mitigation base probably omits "farmland of statewide importance" (each 100 acres = $120,000); two application numbers, two parcel schedules (up to 61.1 acres apart), transposed lease terms, three municipal addresses, two Township Secretaries, an unsigned Decision and an uncertified ordinance excerpt.
8. **Lot coverage may exceed the maximum** — 580 panel acres inside a 720-acre fence is 80.6% before roads and pads, against 75% (540 acres).

## Verification approach

Every total, percentage, rate, threshold and date interval was recomputed rather than accepted (Part D). Thirteen figure recomputations reconcile exactly (DC/AC 1.300; BESS 4.0 h; $6.3M net decommissioning; $7,875,000 security; $747,600 mitigation; $427,000 revenue; $3,208.33/MW; $452.94/acre; and others). Cross-references were machine-checked: every C‑xx and R‑xx reference resolves to an entry, and every register entry is referenced from the matrix.

## Limitations

No hearing transcripts, exhibits, title, survey, soils data or permit records were available, so entries state what the file supports and flag what it does not. The Ordinance text reviewed is an uncertified excerpt that disclaims controlling effect. Legal characterisations (Part I, L‑series) are flagged for confirmation by the Township Solicitor; the document is a compliance instrument, not legal advice.
"}

A working compliance register for Conditional Use Application No. CU‑2024‑006 (Decision and Order dated 6 December 2024), built from all six documents in the file: the Decision, the Zoning Ordinance excerpt (§ 27‑605(B)(14) et seq.), the Lancaster County Planning Commission advisory letter, the Applicant's 1 November 2024 cover letter, and the Township Engineer (10 Jan 2025) and Township Solicitor (15 Jan 2025) emails. Status is stated **as at 15 January 2025**, the date of the most recent source.

## Structure

| Part | Contents |
|---|---|
| 1–2 | Executive summary (snapshot counts, ten headline findings, cross-check against the dissent, priority actions); scope, source inventory, method, status/risk definitions, limitations |
| **Part A** | **Condition compliance tracking matrix** — all 35 conditions, each mapped to its Ordinance provision, responsible party, trigger/deadline, the evidence that would close it, status, risk and cross-references |
| **Part B** | **Ordinance conformance register** — 89 provisions of §§ 27‑602, 27‑605(B)(14) and 27‑605(B)(15) tested against the Decision (31 meets/exceeds, 25 partial, 6 unverified, 9 conflict, 16 not addressed, 2 n/a) |
| **Part C** | **Cross-reference register of inconsistencies** — 55 logged discrepancies with the quoted document values, the quantified variance, the controlling source and the disposition (51 still open) |
| **Part D** | **Independent recomputation schedule** — 39 figures, rates and date intervals recalculated from first principles with the formula shown |
| **Part E** | **Risk register** — 22 risks with likelihood/impact ratings (6 critical, 8 high, 7 medium, 1 low), owners and responses |
| **Part F** | Compliance deadline calendar with derivations and consequences of default |
| **Part G** | 22 open information requests |
| **Part H** | 16 prioritised recommendations with owners and timing |
| **Part I** | Assumptions, legal characterisations (for the Solicitor) and open questions — kept separate from extraction and arithmetic |
| Appendices | Source-to-deliverable traceability, defined terms, revision history and sign-off |

## Most significant findings

1. **Equipment setbacks fall below the Ordinance.** Condition 6 exempts string inverters from the 250 ft property-line setback (100 ft instead — a 60% reduction) and no condition imposes the Ordinance's **500 ft occupied-dwelling setback for substations, inverters and conversion stations** (a 50% shortfall if built to the condition). The Applicant's cover letter repeats the 250 ft figure *as a dwelling setback*, suggesting the error travelled from application into conditions.
2. **The mitigation the Board relied on is narrower than the Ordinance.** Condition 16 covers only north/east boundaries beside residences and omits the roadway-frontage buffers, the 30 ft width, the 60% evergreen floor and the 75%/5-year opacity standard — yet Findings 19 and Conclusions 4 and 6 rest on that screening.
3. **Financial assurances have two start dates.** Conditions 22 and 28 key security and mitigation to the *building* permit; Condition 34 keys them to 60 days before construction. Because the Ordinance defines *grading* permits separately, 850 acres could be cleared before the $7.9M security, the $747,600 payment or the PILOT are in place.
4. **Condition 10 is unperformable as sequenced** — submission by 6 March 2025 after Conservation District approval, where CD review takes 60–90 days (Engineer's estimate); the package would have had to be filed on or about the date of the Decision.
5. **The PILOT blocks every permit and is unresolved**: the Order says the 2% escalator starts after Year 15; the Township wants Year 11 (≈ $118,600 over Years 11–15); the Ordinance's statutory predicate (an exemption/abatement election) is undocumented and recording is not required.
6. **Decommissioning protections are weaker and shorter-fused**: 18-month restoration against the Ordinance's 12; 12 + 18 = 30 months breaches the 24-month absolute cap; 90-day security updates against 60; the 75%-of-gross floor, A.M. Best A‑VII surety rating and Township escrow beneficiary are missing.
7. **Arithmetic and record defects that should be corrected now**: Condition 28 recites 620 acres but pays on 623 ($3,600); the cover letter states a $100,000 operational road bond against the Order's $150,000; the Solicitor's Year 15 figure is $23 low; the mitigation base probably omits "farmland of statewide importance" (each 100 acres = $120,000); two application numbers, two parcel schedules (up to 61.1 acres apart), transposed lease terms, three municipal addresses, two Township Secretaries, an unsigned Decision and an uncertified ordinance excerpt.
8. **Lot coverage may exceed the maximum** — 580 panel acres inside a 720-acre fence is 80.6% before roads and pads, against 75% (540 acres).

## Verification approach

Every total, percentage, rate, threshold and date interval was recomputed rather than accepted (Part D). Thirteen figure recomputations reconcile exactly (DC/AC 1.300; BESS 4.0 h; $6.3M net decommissioning; $7,875,000 security; $747,600 mitigation; $427,000 revenue; $3,208.33/MW; $452.94/acre; and others). Cross-references were machine-checked: every C‑xx and R‑xx reference resolves to an entry, and every register entry is referenced from the matrix.

## Limitations

No hearing transcripts, exhibits, title, survey, soils data or permit records were available, so entries state what the file supports and flag what it does not. The Ordinance text reviewed is an uncertified excerpt that disclaims controlling effect. Legal characterisations (Part I, L‑series) are flagged for confirmation by the Township Solicitor; the document is a compliance instrument, not legal advice.
